chapters.title: Chapter 4130 At the Height of Achievement! I
paragraphs: In the grand and often cruel weavings of existence, there is a fundamental truth that hums beneath every triumph and every tragedy: nothing is more
dangerous than euphoria.
When the path is smooth, when victories follow one another in a graceful, flowing rhythm, that is when existence, with its own cold and indifferent humor, is most likely to deliver a crushing blow.
For in those moments of unbridled success, hubris blooms, and a being, drunk on their own glory, becomes blind to the cracks forming in the foundation they believe to be unshakable.
This bitter lesson was learned most profoundly by the one who was known as THE Living Emotive.
For eons, it had been a being of profound, yet unacknowledged, influence.
The other Living Existences, with their grand authorities of time, space, and order, looked down upon Emotive's shifting, vibrant nature.

They mocked its inability to maintain a single state, its susceptibility to feelings that came and went like the tide. "Out of all of us," THE Living Dimensional had once said with a laugh that bent reality, "you have the least control over existence. We shape reality. You just... feel about it afterward."
These words, and countless others like them, had left a wound. A wound that festered with a singular, driving purpose: to prove them all wrong!

And so, THE Living Emotive embarked on a mission of quiet ambition, one that would not be marked by the grand displays of power favored by its peers, but by an act of profound, and ultimately devastating, cultivation.
For years that stretched into eons, THE Living Emotive searched the vast, expanse of the Earliest Folds, a place where reality was still being defined and rules were not yet etched in stone.
Its form shifted through the full spectrum of feeling, from the blazing joy of a wheel's birth to the cold sorrow of a fold's heart, until it found what it had been seeking.
An Early Creature, a being whose every weaving of existence was a testament to the raw, untamed potential of life!
This creature, known as Soulweaver Magnus, possessed something unique and unprecedented: the highest concentration of THE Creature's Everything of Soul that had ever been observed.

Soulweaver Magnus's very being was a symphony of spiritual authority. His skin shimmered with a light that spoke of a thousand inner lives, and his gaze could touch the essence of any being, knowing them as a book knows its own pages.

THE Living Emotive approached Magnus with a joy that was both a strategy and a genuine expression of admiration. "You are special," it told the Early Creature, its voice a melody of pure awe. "Under my guidance, you could become distinguished to even exceed those who have gained significant parts of THE Creature's Everything. Greater than Gilgamesh with his Everything of Leadership. More profound than Tatiana with her Everything of Dreams."
Magnus, filled with the boundless enthusiasm of youth and the ambition of his kind, felt intoxicated by the promise!

To be guided by one of THE Living Existences themselves was a boon he had not dared to dream of. And so began the long eons of training, a journey not just through power, but through the profound, labyrinthine depths of feeling. THE Living Emotive taught Magnus to wield not just power, but emotion itself, to understand the intricate dance of joy, fear, love, and rage, and to weave these feelings into his very soul.

As centuries turned into millennia, and millennia stretched into epochs, Magnus's power grew to unfathomable heights. His complexity and purity exceeded all conventional metrics, and his soul became a weaving so rich and vibrant it threatened to consume the very concept of soul itself!
And THE Living Emotive, having poured so much of its own existence into this one being, felt something it had never experienced before: pure, unadulterated euphoria.

Its success was a vindication, a glorious rebuttal to all the scorn it had endured. The triumph was so profound, so intensely felt, that it eclipsed everything else. It was, in its mind, the singular most important achievement in all of existence. In its ecstasy, THE Living Emotive made its fatal mistake. It wanted to share this joy, to boast, to prove its worth to the one it still considered a friend.

It left Magnus, if only for a brief moment in the grand scale of time, to find THE Living Origin and bring it back to witness the masterpiece it had crafted. But in its absence, time...that fickle, chaotic river, played its hand. When THE Living Emotive returned with THE Living Origin, its form glowing with the pride of a parent about to show off its brilliant child, it found a scene that shattered its euphoria instantly.
The air, which moments before had pulsed with the quiet harmony of two beings working toward a common goal, was now thick with the competing energies of other Living Existences.

THE Living Spirit, THE Living Dimensional, THE Living Elemental, and others had gathered, a constellation of power and purpose surrounding Magnus. "I have discovered this remarkable Early Creature with the concentrated Everything of Soul," THE Living Spirit was proclaiming, its voice a chorus of whispered truths. "With proper guidance, we could achieve unprecedented things."

THE Living Emotive's form shifted, its euphoria giving way to a white-hot rage. "That's a lie!" it bellowed, its voice shaking the very fabric of the Earliest Folds. "I found him! I've been training him for eons! Ask him yourself- Magnus, tell
them!"
The other Living Existences glanced at one another, their faces a mask of polite indifference.
They were beings of grand scale and even grander ambitions, and to them, such an emotional outburst was, in a word, unseemly.
"Must you be so emotional about everything?" THE Living Dimensional asked, its voice laced with a condescension that felt colder than absolute zero.

It turned its attention to Magnus, its gaze a conceptual scalpel. "Did THE Living Emotive guide you, because if so, we can only leave you to it. If it didn't, then we can offer you the combined support of multiple Living Existences. Just as THE Creature was guided to greatness, we could guide you to be just as great." Magnus looked at THE Living Emotive, his expression a blank canvas. His mentor's form was roiling with a desperate plea, a silent scream of "Tell them! Tell them the truth!"
But Magnus's mind had been swayed by the promise of collective power, a promise more compelling than a single, lonely voice.
In the span of a single heartbeat, he made his choice.
He looked away, and with eyes that held no recognition, no gratitude, no memory, he spoke. "I have never met THE Living Emotive before."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4131 At the Height of Achievement! II
paragraphs: The blatant, impossible lie shattered THE Living Emotive's existence. It stood frozen, unable to process the betrayal.
The euphoria that had elevated it to unimaginable heights was replaced by a crushing despair so profound it threatened to dissolve its very being.

"How pathetic," THE Living Dimensional said, turning back to Emotive with disgust. "Making false claims for credit? You need to do better. Act with the grandeur befitting our station, not this emotional grasping."
"It's unseemly," THE Living Spirit added, its voice a cold whisper. "We are THE Living Existences, not children fighting over toys.

"Perhaps if you focused on actual achievement rather than emotional outbursts," THE Living Elemental suggested, its form solidifying into an immovable pillar of contempt, "you wouldn't need to fabricate accomplishments."
THE Living Emotive stood there, absorbing each word like an arrow to the heart, while its gaze remained locked on Magnus.
The Early Creature it had raised, the one it had loved, now looked through it as if it were nothing more than a ghost.
Even THE Living Origin, its one true friend, shook its head with disappointment and left its side, drawn by the allure of a new and exciting discovery.
In its moment of highest achievement, THE Living Emotive was thrown to its lowest point, what it cared about the most being torn down, and the only friend it had that day was gone.
Such was the cruel, beautiful, and utterly devastating nature of existence!
In the Early Veiled Shore, Noah stood at a peak of a very different kind.
His complexity and purity coursed through him, power that had just crossed into Duke-level territory.
He looked down at the golden sands, where the nine organs of the Primordial Stone Ape rested.
Each one was a monument to a life of unimaginable scale, a treasury of advancement waiting to be claimed.
He looked at the Infiniverse, her green-gold form pulsing with new potential. To Ruination, whose very nature made her perfect for processing destruction into power.
To Sigrid, Order made manifest, ready to organize chaos into strength. To Moiraine, whose paradoxical existence could, perhaps, handle contradictory advancement.

He could attain trillions of complexity and purity from a single organ. Could they not do the same? Could he not produce multiple entities exceeding ten trillion, creating a foundation of power for his Shore that would be unassailable?
The thought blazed through his mind, a beacon of ambition in the glorious light of his Shore.
Four beings of great power, nine organs! They may need one, they may need two. He had enough regardless!
"Infiniverse," he called, his voice carrying the weight of decision.
She floated forward, her form buzzing. "Master?"
"Choose an organ. Any one you feel drawn to."
Her eyes- if the swirling galaxies within her face could be called eyes, widened with understanding.
"The liver," she said without hesitation. "It processes everything, transforms toxins into nutrients. Like how I transform existence into expressions of your will"

Noah nodded, and with a gesture, the golden sands released their hold on the massive hepatic organ. It floated free, crimson-gold and gleaming with stellar radiance, each lobe containing different aspects of the Primordial Stone Ape's accumulated might.
"Ruination."
She stepped forward, her nature already reaching toward the preserved organs with hungry curiosity.
"The spleen," she decided. "It destroys what needs destroying...old cells, foreign invaders. Destruction with purpose. That's what I am."
Another gesture, another organ released. The spleen emerged, condensed immunity and filtered power waiting to be claimed.
"Sigrid."
The Order within her had already been analyzing, calculating, determining optimal choices.
"The kidneys," she said with certainty. "They maintain balance, filter impurities, regulate what stays and what goes. Order in its most fundamental form."
The paired organs rose from their sandy prison, each one containing the filtered wisdom of eons.
"Moiraine."
She approached with the particular grace of someone who existed in multiple states simultaneously.
"The lungs," she chose. "Breath that moved through dimensions, containing both the physical and conceptual. Paradox of needing air in places where air
doesn't exist."
Noah watched as four of his closest allies each claimed an organ worth Folds, worth eons of conventional advancement.
Yet even as he orchestrated this distribution of power, even as he felt his own might settling into Duke-level reality, Khor's warnings echoed in his mind.
Euphoria was existence's favorite time to strike.
The question wasn't if something would go wrong, but when and how
spectacularly.

But for this moment, this brief, shining moment, Noah allowed himself to feel the satisfaction of achievement. His allies would grow stronger. His Shore would become more formidable. His own power had crossed a threshold he'd barely imagined possible days ago.
Tomorrow would bring its own challenges, its own failures, its own reminders that existence didn't care about fair.
Today, though, he would feast on the corpse of impossibility and grow strong enough to face whatever came next.
The Shore hummed with an atmosphere of sacred labor, the golden sands gleaming under the radiant light of the sky.
Moiraine, Ruination, Sigrid, and the Infiniverse stood poised, each of them a conduit for power that transcended the normal bounds of their existence.

The nine organs from the Primordial Stone Ape, each a treasure of concentrated authority, floated before them, awaiting their purpose. But even amidst this scene of creation and growth, a silence fell over the shoreline as Khor floated toward Noah.
Her diminutive form, a contradiction of primordial power and fragile appearance, moved with a grace that made the very air seem to part for her.
She came to rest beside him, her gaze traveling from his face to the nine organs awaiting consumption.
"Outsider," she said, her voice a whisper that carried across the vast expanse of the Shore, "since things seem to have settled down, I shall take the Early Veiled
Shore to the level of a Radiant Shore."
Her words were simple, yet they held the weight of a monumental undertaking.

This wasn't merely an act of will; it was a promise that she, in her diminished state, would call upon the deep, forgotten weavings of inevitability to accelerate the Shore's evolution how she remembered!
It was an act of power she likely hadn't wielded since before her cessation.

Noah nodded, but his eyes were not on her or the Shore. His focus, his entire attention, was on Ozymandias. His other self, now a terrifying nexus of pure hunger, was permeating the upper body of the Primordial Stone Ape!

chapters.title: Chapter 4132 This, I Swear! I
paragraphs: Where the heart had been, where the organs had been, Ozymandias was weaving himself into the very fabric of the corpse.

His tendrils of obsidian-gold, each a filament of insatiable hunger, extended across the ape's colossal body, tracing the veins and arteries, replacing sinew with void, and bone with the concept of recursion!
Within the ape's body, a world of resources waited. The brain, a mass of pure complexity that had processed thoughts of quadrillions, was a meal of unimaginable significance.
The digestive tract, which had broken down concepts as easily as food, contained the wisdom of internal alchemy.
The skeletal structure, harder than conceptual diamond, was a potential treasure trove of structural marrow!

Ozymandias's tentacles found their way to the brain first, and Noah felt a wave of pure thought, uncorrupted by emotion or memory, flow through their bond. The consumption was a clinical, terrifying process.
There was no joy, no rage, no pleasure...only the perfect, efficient conversion of complexity into purity.
The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Brain
Purity Gained: +5,000,000,000,000 (+5 Trillion)|
A wave of radiant black light erupted from Ozymandias as his purity surged, his form becoming more defined, his tentacles growing denser with insatiable purpose!
The purity from the brain was followed by the devouring of the digestive tract. The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Digestive Tract
Purity Gained: +4,500,000,000,000 (+4.5 Trillion)|
The prompt was relentless, each one detailing the consumption of another organ or body part, another leap in power for Ozymandias.

The skeletal structure yielded the greatest gain, its immense toughness and history of resisting entropy converting into a staggering amount of purity. The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Skeletal Structure]
Purity Gained: +6,500,000,000,000 (+6.5 Trillion)|
HUUM!
Khor, who had watched this terrifying ballet of consumption with a knowing smile, floated closer to Noah.
She reached out and, with a touch so light it was almost not there, began to run her hand through his hair. It was an act of ancient affection, an elder stroking the head of a fledgling.

"You play with death, Outsider," she said, her voice a soft hum that resonated directly in his soul, "but you must be careful when playing with the Dead. The Truly Dead Existences... are those that never stay dead, even after their existence is collapsed."
She paused, her touch becoming more insistent, as if she were trying to impart lesson through touch alone.

"Their way of existence is to be. To be, regardless of being alive or not. They are a principle in and of themselves. They hunger for life, but they do not fear death, for death is not an ending to them. They know that even if their physical form is shattered, they will always find a way to be. They are inevitable. And what you seek to do... what you seek to do with that corpse... will it achieve that?"

Her question hung in the air, a chilling note of caution in the symphony of his ambition. She was asking if he, through his acts of necromancy and death, could truly create something that was akin to Dead Existences!
Noah looked down at his primary existence, at his hands that were now capable of holding the weight of existence, and his eyes burned with fierce resolve.
He would answer her question with action!
With Ozymandias, he would light up a shell, a puppet of death, with life itself!
He would achieve the impossible, as he always did!

Khor's hand fell from Noah's head, and with her final word of warning spoken, she moved away. The golden sands of the Shore began to glow with a strange, otherworldly light as she started her work, accelerating its evolution through her unique understanding of inevitability.
At the same time, the colossal, half-eaten corpse of the Primordial Stone Ape, still stuck upright in the sand, began to move.
Countless black tentacles, obsidian and glistening, erupted from the lower body that Noah had not had time to claim..
The tendrils wove themselves together with meticulous, horrifying precision, rebuilding the ape's massive form.
Flesh was replaced with hunger, bone with the concept of recurrence. The Obsidian tentacles even mimicked the fur-like quality and look of the ape's original state, a grotesque imitation of life.
The shell was being made, and soon, Noah would light it up with the glory of Necromancy and Death!
And then-
BOOM!
The skies of the Early Veiled Shore, and the entire Infiniverse, trembled.
A soundless tear, a rent in the fabric of existence, opened far above them!
A terrifying white light, a beam of pure authority and immense complexity, shot
through the wound!
It was so sudden!
Such a quick change as when he looked up, Noah recognized the ageness and
oldness of this light.
It was unimaginably powerful and ancient, something from the Earliest Folds, and before it, Noah was nothing!
Something...from the Earliest Folds!
The light descended with a silent inevitability that made all of time slow down, as if Existence itself was holding its breath. It was a strike meant to kill. A killing
blow!
Noahs eyes pulsed with a terrifying glory, his body erupting with every possible ounce of his complexity.
He roared within, a guttural bellow of pure Tyranny, as he surged forward to meet the terrifying light!
The Haki that had just begun to form within his heart exploded outwards, a wave of defiance against the crushing pressure.
He could instinctively sense that he was the target. The light had come for him.
And so he flew up, not to escape, but to meet it, to ensure that his family would
not be affected, that nobody would die!
He did not ask how it had found him. He did not ask why.
He moved on instinct!
On the ground, Ozymandias, his tentacled form still intertwined with the ape's
corpse, was frozen mid-process.
He was chained by the immense power of the attack, unable to move, unable to
leave.
This was happening in a single, prolonged second.
And yet, in that same stretched moment of time...many arose to defend him.
First, the Infiniverse materialized beside Noah.
Her body, shining with a myriad of lights, surged forward, her eyes blazing with
a lividity that would make the Royal Living Existences tremble.
Her hand shot out, intending to give all of herself, to use her entire existence as
a shield for her master!

There was no joy, no rage, no pleasure...only the perfect, efficient conversion of complexity into purity.
The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Brain
Purity Gained: +5,000,000,000,000 (+5 Trillion)|
A wave of radiant black light erupted from Ozymandias as his purity surged, his form becoming more defined, his tentacles growing denser with insatiable purpose!
The purity from the brain was followed by the devouring of the digestive tract.
The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Digestive Tract
Purity Gained: +4,500,000,000,000 (+4.5 Trillion)|
The prompt was relentless, each one detailing the consumption of another organ or body part, another leap in power for Ozymandias.
The skeletal structure yielded the greatest gain, its immense toughness and history of resisting entropy converting into a staggering amount of purity.
The Purest Hunger Consumes: Primordial Skeletal Structure]
Purity Gained: +6,500,000,000,000 (+6.5 Trillion)|
HUUM!
Khor, who had watched this terrifying ballet of consumption with a knowing smile, floated closer to Noah.
She reached out and, with a touch so light it was almost not there, began to run her hand through his hair.
It was an act of ancient affection, an elder stroking the head of a fledgling.
"You play with death, Outsider," she said, her voice a soft hum that resonated directly in his soul, "but you must be careful when playing with the Dead.
The Truly Dead Existences... are those that never stay dead, even after their existence is collapsed."
She paused, her touch becoming more insistent, as if she were trying to impart lesson through touch alone.
"Their way of existence is to be.
To be, regardless of being alive or not.
They are a principle in and of themselves.
They hunger for life, but they do not fear death, for death is not an ending to them.
They know that even if their physical form is shattered, they will always find a way to be.
They are inevitable.
And what you seek to do... what you seek to do with that corpse... will it achieve that?"
Her question hung in the air, a chilling note of caution in the symphony of his ambition.
She was asking if he, through his acts of necromancy and death, could truly create something that was akin to Dead Existences!
Noah looked down at his primary existence, at his hands that were now capable of holding the weight of existence, and his eyes burned with fierce resolve.
He would answer her question with action!
With Ozymandias, he would light up a shell, a puppet of death, with life itself!
He would achieve the impossible, as he always did!
Khor's hand fell from Noah's head, and with her final word of warning spoken, she moved away.
The golden sands of the Shore began to glow with a strange, otherworldly light as she started her work, accelerating its evolution through her unique understanding of inevitability.
At the same time, the colossal, half-eaten corpse of the Primordial Stone Ape, still stuck upright in the sand, began to move.
Countless black tentacles, obsidian and glistening, erupted from the lower body that Noah had not had time to claim..
The tendrils wove themselves together with meticulous, horrifying precision, rebuilding the ape's massive form.
Flesh was replaced with hunger, bone with the concept of recurrence.
The Obsidian tentacles even mimicked the fur-like quality and look of the ape's original state, a grotesque imitation of life.
The shell was being made, and soon, Noah would light it up with the glory of Necromancy and Death!
And then-
BOOM!
The skies of the Early Veiled Shore, and the entire Infiniverse, trembled.
A soundless tear, a rent in the fabric of existence, opened far above them!
A terrifying white light, a beam of pure authority and immense complexity, shot
through the wound!
It was so sudden!
Such a quick change as when he looked up, Noah recognized the ageness and
oldness of this light.
It was unimaginably powerful and ancient, something from the Earliest Folds, and before it, Noah was nothing!
Something...from the Earliest Folds!
The light descended with a silent inevitability that made all of time slow down, as if Existence itself was holding its breath.
It was a strike meant to kill.
A killing
blow!
Noahs eyes pulsed with a terrifying glory, his body erupting with every possible ounce of his complexity.
He roared within, a guttural bellow of pure Tyranny, as he surged forward to meet the terrifying light!
The Haki that had just begun to form within his heart exploded outwards, a wave of defiance against the crushing pressure.
He could instinctively sense that he was the target.
The light had come for him.
And so he flew up, not to escape, but to meet it, to ensure that his family would
not be affected, that nobody would die!
He did not ask how it had found him.
He did not ask why.
He moved on instinct!
On the ground, Ozymandias, his tentacled form still intertwined with the ape's
corpse, was frozen mid-process.
He was chained by the immense power of the attack, unable to move, unable to
leave.
This was happening in a single, prolonged second.
And yet, in that same stretched moment of time...many arose to defend him.
First, the Infiniverse materialized beside Noah.
Her body, shining with a myriad of lights, surged forward, her eyes blazing with
a lividity that would make the Royal Living Existences tremble.
Her hand shot out, intending to give all of herself, to use her entire existence as
a shield for her master!

chapters.title: Chapter 4133 This, I swear! II
paragraphs: Then, Ruination appeared. A crimson wheel of endings materialized around her, and she bellowed, directing all her possible endings, all her immense power, to meet the impending strike!
Above them all, Moiraine paradoxically appeared, her eyes shining with a
paradoxical rage. She began to burn her very paradoxical nature for power, her form a beacon of defiance.
Even further above, Sigrid appeared as if Order had ordained for her to be at the forefront.
Her face was a mask of cold fury, her forehead splitting open as a bony Eye of Order, a resplendent white pupil at its center, rose to meet the attack.

It shot out a beam of Order, a pure, white light to oppose the killing strike. And then, a howl. Yoshinami's spider form appeared beside them, her many eyes shining with a terrible defiance as she howled out war cry that transcended sound!
An illusion of Heidrun, her lustrous white-gold fur glowing, appeared beside Yoshinami, her hooves raised in a gesture of challenge!
Titano's simple eyes remained simple, but he slapped his chest with a boom that created tremors in the air, and began to enlarge, his form seeking to encompass and cover everyone.
All of them arose. They could all die, but he could not. Not their Master, not the one who had brought them to this glorious place!
Noah saw all of this in slow motion, his existence howling, raging at the absurdity of it all.
And worst of all, in that moment of collective defiance... his mother, Amelia Osmont, appeared beside him.
Beside him!
She had no immense power, no special abilities to offer.
She was simply his mother.
But her presence was a truth that could not be denied, a vulnerability that Noah could not bear.
"OOOH!"
He howled out with all of his existence!
Waves of blue mana, a sea of infinite mana, erupted from his body.
Infinite. Expanding. Pure!
No Fear. No Doubt!
They were filled with emotion, with rage, a rage that asked, Why? Why, after he had done everything, had he not been enough?
Why, after he had given everything, was he still powerless in the face of this immense light?!
And then, his mind buzzed with a singular thought.
He... had not given everything. Not his Everything. Not yet.
For his family. For his people. For himself. He would give Everything in exchange for their survival.
"I give..." he began to speak, his voice a roaring declaration against the inevitable.
But then, a sigh. It echoed out, a sound of immense sadness, and a small figure, Khor, appeared above everyone.
Her eyes were filled with a chilly, melancholic light as she looked upon the scene with a profound distaste.
"Gilgamesh," she uttered, the name a curse on her lips.
Her small figure moved ahead of everyone, appearing as a delicate, almost ethereal being in the face of the massive, terrifying white light.
She opened her mouth.
And with a sense of sadness, of melancholy so deep it would drown the soul, she said, "I Hunger. Therefore I am."
BOOOM!
The light of the killing strike crashed down. The small figure of Khor ate up nearly all of it, her mouth an abyss of inevitability that consumed not just light, but the very authority of the attack.
But a portion of the light was too fast, too pure in its malice. It phased through her, a tiny, almost infinitesimal fraction of the original beam.
It was so small, so insignificant, yet it smashed into Noah.
BOOM!
His figure was flung back, and he crashed onto the Early Veiled Shore, creating a massive indentation and crack in the golden sand.
The white light disappeared, and an immense silence settled over the Shore.
All eyes, wide with horror and a dawning understanding of what had just transpired, were on Khor in the skies, and Noah down below.
In the skies was Khor.
She looked...unbelievably frail. After she had swallowed that light, her skin expanded and then contracted as if millions of needles had erupted from within.
Obsidian-crimson blood gushed from her, and her figure seemed desolate,
lifeless.
She began to fall, like a feather from a broken wing!
And down below...
Noah felt an immense, terrifying pain coursing throughout his existence as he
was battered by the attack that felt like a branding.
The pain was not a physical one...it was a conceptual, synaptic pain that transcended any sensation he had ever experienced.
It was the pain of his very essence being violated by a strike that was never
meant for him, and a blow that his power could not defend against.
But he was not looking at the prompts that were now filling his vision, his
entire focus was on Khor.
You have avoided complete collapse regardless of how many paradoxical lives
you could have given up.
Across countless distances, the degraded authority of The First Leader, Gilgamesh, was left idle seeking the signature of your existence, and it had
finaly found you now.
[This authority had been degrading for eons, but was still enough to achieve the
bidding of Gilgamesh who was curious of the entity who seemed to traverse across Folds themlseves.
This authority was merely that...of curiosity as it was not even a true attack.
Nearly all of it was devoured by Khor, the First Hunger.
A small portion struck you as on your existence, the Curse of Curiosity of The First Leader has been branded onto you.
This curse reduces the power of your existence and Everything permanently by half until the curiosity of the First Leader is satiated.
Negative effects include: Inability to forge new Glyphs, reduced effectiveness of existing distinctions, and a constant, low-grade existential hum of curiosity
following your every move.
The prompts were heavy.
But even in the face of these terrifying prompts, his eyes remained locked on
Khor.
He flew out of the crater, his existence howling with rage, towards her delicate,
broken form.
All of those who rose to defend him looked on with maddened, somber eyes.
Silence. Not a single voice rang out. It was as if existence itself was mourning the sacrifice of a being that had chosen to be a shield, to protect what it had just found!

chapters.title: Chapter 4134 This, I Swear! III
paragraphs: And in the midst of all this...
"Don't announce my time of death just yet, Outsider."
WAA!
A weak voice echoed out!
It was weak, but there.
The silence that fell upon the Shore was heavy, suffocating.
The air itself seemed to have stopped its flow, holding its breath in the face of what had just transpired.
Across the golden sands, every being stood frozen, a tableau of somberness and shock etched upon their faces!
All eyes were on the small figure of Khor, now a delicate, broken feather drifting down from the sky.
Noah, his own body aflame with a searing, unfamiliar pain, moved with a grace born of lividity.
He flew upward, his tyrannical will overcoming the agony that threatened to unmake him. He reached for her, his arms an anchor in the maelstrom of his own suffering.
As his hands closed around her, a faint sense of life, a weak spark of her immense being, returned to him.

He cradled her, his gaze sweeping over her riddled body, which seemed to be made of shattered starlight and obsidian shards. Her skin, once so vibrant, was now a pale, desolate canvas of countless wounds.
He looked into her eyes, and there, amidst the fracturing of her consciousness, he saw a weak smile.

"I won't be leaving just yet, Outsider," she whispered, her voice a brittle echo of its former power. "I told you existence was unfair, I just did not expect to be used as an example so soon to make this point."
Her words, though weak, carried the familiar weight of her ancient wisdom.

He held her close, ignoring the constant, burning agony that coursed through his existence- a pain that felt as if his very soul was being set aflame to satiate the monstrous curiosity of a being he had never even met.
He looked up at the sky, his eyes, filled with a primal, untamed fury, affirming that nothing else could possibly come down!
The tyranny in his gaze was a physical force, a silent promise of vengeance against a foe who had, with a single, idle act, reduced him to this state of burning agony.

In his arms, Khor's voice, though still weak, echoed out again. "That authority, that attack really, was a cognizant bundle of Authority that Gilgamesh left out countless years ago in the Earliest Folds...after your departure from the Verdant Eternia Tribe. It held no more true cognizance and was not even connected to him anymore as he won't even know that it finally found its target cycles of time later. You and your Early Veiled Shore... should be safe, Outsider."

She continued to speak, her voice fading in and out like a dying ember. "I just got back, swallowing something filled with identity and purpose like that authority of Gilgamesh was akin to my existence taking in something it could not fully contain early. It was painful, but after my existence stabilizes, my Hunger will digest what I swallowed as I will be greater than I was before. Existence is unfair, yes, but all those points of hardships will also pave way for opportunity. This will be mine. For you... a bit of that authority still touched you as it should be limiting your existence tremendously, but even that... could be an opportunity. You just have to find out how to make that pain into opportunity."
He held her figure close, his eyes burning with a terrible resolve!
Around them, the others slowly began to stir, their shock giving way to a dawning comprehension of what had just occurred.
They gathered around Noah and Khor, a circle of silent, grieving protectors!
Khor, seeing their solemn faces, smiled faintly.
"Why are you gathering as if there is a funeral? Go on and go back to doing your things."
An immense silence remained.
The Shore, once so vibrant, seemed to have been muted, its light dimmed by a shared horror.
It was then that a figure, cloaked in a blinding white light, moved through the crowd.
Sigrid, her forehead still split, the Eye of Order pulsating with a brilliant, cold light, knelt down beside Khor.

Her gaze was steady, unwavering, and as she spoke, her voice carried the weight of a fundamental law. "Since you seek to stabilize your existence before you can process what you hungered... then I shall impose that stability. If I cannot do it, am I truly Order?"
BOOM!
A terrifying white light, a beam of pure, absolute Order, erupted from the eye on Sigrid's forehead.
It bathed Khor in its brilliance, the weavings of THE Living Order truly and fully drenching one of the oldest Inevitabilities in existence.
Sigrid's voice rang out, a command that reality itself would obey. "Be ordered. Be stable!"
The brilliant light paved the way for glory.
Khor's body illuminated, the countless wounds on her disappearing as her form began to float and shine with waves of pure, obsidian light.
The process of her healing, of her reconstitution, was underway, a testament to the power of Order imposed upon chaos.
Khor's form, now floating in a cocoon of obsidian light, began to heal.
She shook her head, a soft, tired sigh escaping her lips.

She looked at Sigrid and Noah, her voice a brittle whisper, "When something heavy occurs, turn them into gains and keep moving forward. My existence is digesting the hunger right now and moving forward, what about you all?"
Noah listened to her words, the burning pain of the curse a constant reminder of his helplessness.
He looked down at Khor, at the small figure that had given up so much for him, and his eyes blazed with a profound, tyrannical fury!
His gaze swept over the others, his people, his family, who had risked everything for him.
"I do not know Gilgamesh," Noah's voice rang out, his words a terrifying, imposing declaration against all of existence.

"I do not know whether Gilgamesh is alive or dead. But whether alive, whether dead, I swear upon my own existence itself that I will be the one... to collapse the weavings of Existence of The First Leader, Gilgamesh! That... is a promise!"
BOOM!
He spoke the words as if he were swearing them on his own existence, and all of surrounding existence listened.
Khor heard them. All others present heard them. The promise hung in the air, a physical weight of vengeance and fury.
Noah's gaze remained bright as he turned to look at all of those who had risen to defend him.
His eyes fell upon his mother, Amelia Osmont, who, upon seeing his livid gaze, sighed tenderly and did not tell him to calm.
She instead nodded with a fierceness that matched his own, her eyes flashing with a tyrannical fury.
Noah nodded in return. He would make good on his promise.
He began to walk towards the corpse of the ape, where Ozymandias was still intricately connected.
He closed his eyes, feeling the relentless, burning hum of the curse spreading across his existence, a constant reminder of Gilgamesh's power.
A curse? On his existence? His eyes flashed with a tyrannical light.
He would not stand for this. Existence was unfair? Okay! He would show existence just how unfair he could be!
As he stood before Ozymandias, waves of tyranny rose over his body like never before.
He locked eyes with his other self, his voice a low, dangerous growl. "Hunger for the restraints that bind me. Devour... this miserable curse of The First Leader!"
HUUM!
He would use his own weavings to unmake a curse placed upon him, a final act of defiance against a universe that sought to humble him.
As he stood there, his body filled with a burning, terrible resolve, thousands of tentacles from Ozymandias came to surround him, eager to obey their Master's will!
Adui

He would show existence just how unfair he could be!
As he stood before Ozymandias, waves of tyranny rose over his body like never before.
He locked eyes with his other self, his voice a low, dangerous growl.
"Hunger for the restraints that bind me.
Devour... this miserable curse of The First Leader!"
HUUM!
He would use his own weavings to unmake a curse placed upon him, a final act of defiance against a universe that sought to humble him.
As he stood there, his body filled with a burning, terrible resolve, thousands of tentacles from Ozymandias came to surround him, eager to obey their Master's will!
Adui
Creator's Thoughts

chapters.title: Chapter 4135 Hunger and Suffering! I
paragraphs: Silence reigned on the golden sands, a heavy, somber quiet that was more profound than any noise.
The Shore, a place of perpetual vibrancy, had been muted by the shock of the attack and Khor's sacrifice. Yet, at the heart of this stillness, a whirlwind of power was beginning to form.
Noah stood before the bisected body of the Primordial Stone Ape, which now had a writhing, obsidian-gold lower half made up entirely of Ozymandias's tentacles.
Thousand of tentacles, each one a tendril of insatiable hunger, wrapped around Noah's form, not to harm him, but to serve him.
Their purpose was singular, their hunger absolute: to devour the curse placed upon their master by The First Leader, Gilgamesh.
Others watched from a distance, their faces a mixture of solemnity.
The memory of the terrifying white light, of Khor's sacrifice, was still too fresh, too raw, for them to fully comprehend what was happening.

They saw the tentacles surrounding Noah, and while they knew their purpose, the sight was still a terrifying reminder of the thin line between this Shore's life and the ever-present threat of oblivion.
Noah's eyes, however, were not on the crowd, nor on Ozymandias.
They were on the runic prompts that had been waiting for his attention, prompts he had put on hold to focus on the immediate, tangible danger.
Now, with the threat momentarily abated, his gaze, burning with a furious, untamed tyranny, fell upon them.
|The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest has witnessed the tremendous effort that the natives of your Early Veiled Shore put in when faced with an unprecedented attack.|
|Such an effort, a collective bond forged in the face of annihilation, is deemed a rare and critical harvest. It is the perfect soil for a Principle to grow in.|
|Due to this, the percentage of maturation for the Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest has jumped from 3% to 10%!|
The number, ten percent, buzzed with the force of an existential declaration.
In existence where progress was measured in infinitesimal increments, this was a leap of astronomical proportions.
It meant that Noah's ability to manipulate the fundamental principle of effort and reward was no longer a trickle, but a veritable torrent.
|At 10% Maturation, new capabilities have been unlocked.|

|The Resistance of Perpetual Harvest has also reached 10%. Your existence is now ten times more expensive for reality to oppose. Attacks against you require an additional 1000% effort from the aggressor. You are a walking paradox of defensive endurance.|

|You can now forge up to ten Glyphs of the Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest, up from the previous three. The cost is being scaled up to a heavy 500 billion in Complexity and Purity, but the boons will be amplified a hundredfold.|
|The Perpetual Growth Field can now cover the entire Shore and beyond, reaching into adjacent Folds, its power to accelerate development growing with every second.|

|You have been granted a new distinction: The Shield of Unity. You are recognized as one who can foster an unbreakable bond in the face of existential threats. This distinction amplifies the effectiveness of the Perpetual Harvest Principle, especially in a collective setting.|
Noah's tyrannical gaze deepened as he absorbed the information.
The boons were staggering, a reward so immense it dwarfed the pain of the curse still burning within him.
But he knew, with a cold certainty that transcended emotion, that he could not enjoy them yet.
The curse had to be dealt with first. A parasite, a limitation imposed by an enemy he hadn't even met, could not be allowed to fester. It had to be unmade.
He focused again on a new set of prompts, a different kind of reward, one born of Khor's sacrifice.
|Due to the extraordinary effort done by Khor, The First Hunger, the Symbolic Heart of Hunger within you has been enriched further.|

|The Nine Seals of The First Hunger are now capable of being visualized. When all nine seals are released, the true, undiminished power of The First Hunger, held since the Earliest Folds, will be unleashed.|
|Due to the recent devouring of the degraded authority of The First Leader, the first seal is nearly broken. The only remaining condition is the swallowing of the Everything of an Entire Fold.|

|The First Seal, The Seal of Primordial Appetites, yearns for a meal that defines its hunger. It seeks an essence of life so vast, so complete, that its consumption would shake the very foundations of existence.|
A Fold. A single, entire Fold. The thought blazed in Noah's mind.
The complexity, the sheer scale of such a task, was astronomical. It was a meal that would break a normal being's mind, a consumption that would make other's feeding look like a child's snack.
But Noah knew exactly where to get a meal of that scale.
The Nullvein Gravewake Folds!
This was a Fold that had already been moved by a Royal Living Existence!
A Fold he could reach as he was in it, a Fold he could provide. Od course, he would see to it that her Hunger could encompass the Fold, but not the countless lifeforms and Wheels inside of it.
Those could simply be relocated into the vast Osmontian Shore!
He would not just feed his hunger, he would unleash a primordial appetite that would make the Foldless Ones tremble!
The endless hum of Ozymandias's hunger permeated Noah's mind, a ceaseless, ravenous drone that now sought the very thing that was causing its master's pain.
It located the markers of the curse, the tiny, insidious threads of Gilgamesh's authority that had woven themselves into Noah's very essence.
The hum became a roar, a silent, all-consuming bellow of "Food."
Noah looked out at the others, his gaze burning with a profound tyranny. He was almost harmed. His family alingside him.
And his body...how dare The First Leader think he could impose such a thing?!
He would not stand for this. His existence was his own, his body his own temple, his authority his own law!
No mere authority, especially one that had been dormant for eons, could curse him and remain so.
He bellowed, a roar that shook the very foundations of the Shore and the Infiniverse itself.
"Feel the hunger! Be devoured! Begone!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4136 Hunger and Suffering! II
paragraphs: The ravenous scene was a symphony of chaos and consumption.
The thousands of tentacles that surrounded Noah suddenly developed millions of obsidian-gold teeth.
They snapped shut around him, biting down on something invisible within his existence. The air crackled, the Shore buzzed, as if all these teeth were grinding on an immovable, unmakable force.
The invisible thing was unfathomably hard. A curse, a brand from a being of 500+ quadrillion complexity, could not be so easily consumed even if it was an infinitesmal shred!
Some of Ozymandias's teeth cracked, shattered under the strain. But the tentacles, the very essence of inevitability, would not be denied.
Even more teeth reformed, and they continued biting and grinding down. The endless hunger of Ozymandias, The Purest Hunger, had begun to eat away at even this authority.
The process was arduous. Noah's eyes radiated waves of pure, untamed tyranny as he bellowed, his voice a roaring command that echoed across the Shore.
"Begone!"
BOOM!
A white light, a brilliant spark of primordial authority, fizzled and broke from him.
Noah felt a sense of immense liberation, as if massive locks, placed upon him not long ago, had been released.
His existence blazed with majesty, and white, gold, and blue waves of light surged around him, a testament to his newfound freedom!
|You have successfully devoured a curse that lesser beings would have simply accepted and been shackled by! Your will has bent a rule of existence and remade it.|

|The tremendous effort of this act has been recognized and rewarded. Your existence has proven its tyranny, its relentless refusal to be defined by the will of others, especially The First Leader, Gilgamesh|

|The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest rewards this effort with a massive, one time boom after its 10% maturation. Your personal gains from this act: +5,000,000,000,000 (+5 Trillion) Complexity and Purity. A testament to a truly quintessentially tyrannical act.|

|Ozymandias devoured the Curse to attain: +15,000,000,000,000 (+15 Trillion) Purity! The curse, a manifestation of a being's will, was a meal of unprecedented significance. Its essence has now been converted into pure, undiluted purity.|
|The terrifying quality of the Curse of The First Leader flowed into Ozymandias and the corpse he is currently connected to... and it caused an unintended reaction.|
Noah's gaze on the prompts was a silent, incandescent calm.
He had been branded, his power reduced by half, by a being's curiosity.

He had been a plaything, a subject of a cruel curiosity. But he had not accepted it. He had fought back, he had devoured the curse itself. He had shown existence just how unfair he could be...and this was just the start!
His eyes, burning with a cold, tyrannical light, landed on the Primordial Stone Ape's corpse.
His Necromancy and Death Towers of Osmont had manifested around it, their forms a silent, glowing promise of a future yet to come.
The ape's massive pupils, once a flat, dead grey, now radiated a terrifying light.
The rage they had died with, a furious, undiluted anger, had begun to change. It was no longer the pain of a victim, but the fury of a warrior preparing for war.

|A convergence of unexpected events and authorities has occurred. The Primordial Stone Ape, infused with the essence of Gilgamesh's curse and the pure hunger of an Inevitability, is returning as... a Dead Existential Inevitability due to its bindings with Ozymandias, a unique type of Dead Existence!|
A Dead Existential Inevitability. A being of paradox, of hunger, of death, of life, of rage. The perfect weapon.
Noah read the prompts, and a terrifying, triumphant calm spread across his face.
"Merely the Curse of Curiosity! Merely The Curse of an Early Creature! I devour this today, and I will devour the one who sent it in the future!"
BOOM!
Noah's gaze, heavy with the weight of recent suffering and the promise of vengeance, focused entirely on the Primordial Stone Ape.
It was no longer a mere corpse, nor a simple puppet of hunger.
It was a Dead Existential Inevitability, a being born from a convergence of factors that defied all logic and precedent!
Through the intricate web of Ozymandias's tentacles, which had spread like a parasitic growth across the ape's massive form, Noah could feel every pulse of this terrible, new life.
He felt the immense power that, even in death, still resided within the ape's essence- a power that, though diminished by his consumption of its organs, was now being reignited.
The very air around the corpse began to hum, not with the familiar energies of a living existence, but with a unique and terrifying authority...Early Dead Existential Authority.
It was almost the same silent, obsidian dread he had sensed from the Primordial Death that had been annihilated by Yoshinami, an authority that transcended the simple rules of life and death.
Almost...but not really.
This had a feel of Age. Oldness.
Early!
Noah's eyes, a maelstrom of calm and glory, flashed as prompts bloomed in his mind, their words a testament to the unprecedented thing that was rising through his hands.
|Through Ozymandias, the Dead Existential Inevitability- Primordial Stone Ape, opens its eyes once more.|

|It is an extremely unique Existence, bearing the distinction of The Dead- two words that carry a meaning very few understand. The Dead do not stay dead; their Way of Existence is to be. Even if their weavings are collapsed again and again and again, they will always reform.|
HUUM!
His mind raced, a cold, tyrannical certainty taking root.
The many Dead Existences that had been decimated in the Transcendent Temporal Folds were not gone forever.

It seemed that all of them, in their own time and their own way, would invariably return. He felt a fleeting urge to revisit that spot, to witness their inevitable return, to understand if they would simply reappear where they fell, or if their rebirth was a more chaotic, unpredictable force.
The thought was pushed aside as he focused on the rising, terrifying obsidian authority around Ozymandias.
The aura of death was both terrifying and regal, a silent promise of an existence that defied cessation.

chapters.title: Chapter 4137 Hunger and Suffering! III
paragraphs: Sigrid, her entire being bathed in the white light of Order, frowned as she looked at the ape's shifting form, the authority it emanated a direct affront to her very nature.

Even Khor, whose form was still a beacon of reconstituting light, showed a flicker of genuine surprise in her eyes. She had not expected to see the authority of a Dead Existence manifest so completely!
The obsidian authority reached a precipice of concentration, and the ape's eyes, once dead and lifeless, snapped open.
They shone with an obsidian-gold light, currently devoid of the ape's original cognizance. They held a new, singular gaze: the terrible, hungry will of Ozymandias.
Prompts bloomed, detailing the monumental effort and its unprecedented result.

|This is a tremendous effort, supported by the Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest, because harvest does not pick and choose between life and death; it permeates all existence. One can have harvest permeate across existence.|

|Your Necromancy and Death Towers of Osmont burn with power and recognition, their aid, along with Cheats and all other Vital Lighthouses of the Early Atlas of the Folds, have brought about an unprecedented result.|
| As of this moment, your Legion of Dead Existences has gained its first member.|
Noah's eyes on the prompts were a silent, incandescent flash of triumph.
The Seed of Perpetual Harvest had rewarded his effort, his tyrannical will, by allowing him to harvest a life not of his own, to command a being of death and hunger.
The fusion of his will with Ozymandias's hunger, and the raw authority of the ape's corpse, had created something that should not exist!
A Legion of Dead Existences, and this creature was its first member.
He would not be defined by the rules of Existence; he would bend them to his will!
The prompts continued to cascade, each one a testament to his growing power.
|The Dead Existential Inevitability, Primordial Stone Ape, has officially been born.|
|Primordial Stone Ape(Dead Existential Inevitability)|
|Complexity: 200,000,000,000,000 (200 Trillion)|
|Purity: 0 (All converted to Complexity to fuel its necrotic state)|
|Distinctions:|
|The Dead- A state of existence that defies cessation. The creature will reform even if its weavings are completely collapsed.|
|Inevitability- The hunger of existence made manifest. It devours and grows, fueled by any existence it consumes.|
|Necrotic Inevitability- A unique fusion of hunger and death. It can consume both life and death, converting all matter and essence into its own power.|
|Early Butcher- A title inherited from Ozymandias, now an innate skill. It can dissect any being of immense power with a terrifying efficiency.|
Noah's eyes, burning with a cold, tyrannical light, landed on the Primordial Stone Ape.
A single act of a being he hadn't even met, an act of sheer curiosity, had reduced him to a state of burning agony.
But now, that act, that curse, had been devoured and in its place, he had created something that would shake the very foundations of his current existence!
The ape began to move, its body shifting with a grace that seemed both dead and alive. Its eyes, which had once held the terrifying will of Ozymandias, blinked.
And then, as if a veil had been lifted, it gained a return of its own sense of cognizance. The terrifying power of The Dead flowed through it, an aura of utter regal darkness.

The countless tentacles of Ozymandias left the ape's body, and yet, brand new tentacles, formed of obsidian Early Dead Existential Authority, sprouted forth, weaving themselves into a terrifying new form.
The ape's lower body, once a mass of tentacles, became more and more real, its form now a brilliant obsidian-gold, with fur-like qualities that emanated profound waves of death.
It was a beautiful, horrifying creation, a perfect synthesis of life and death, of life and inevitability.
Ozymandias floated beside Noah, the two bodies standing side by side, a terrifying mirror of tyrannical power.
They looked upon this unique Dead Existence they had brought to fruition. And in that moment, the ape, filled with the new cognizance of a being born of death and hunger, knelt.

Its massive hand rose to its chest and tapped three times, a greeting given to Early Creatures. A gesture of submission and respect from a being of unfathomable power, a testament to the might of The Early Creature, Osmont!
On this day, Noah, for the first time, received the greeting given to Early Creatures from a Dead Existence that he had brought to fruition.
It was a victory born of suffering, a triumph forged in the fires of a curse!
Suffering.
A unique idea that seemed always present, but it became moreso at a point in time in distant past.
In the Earliest Folds, where the glorious potential of existence swirled and coalesced into form, a time existed when THE Creature's power grew so immense that its presence became a choice.
Even THE Living Existences, those who wielded the fundamental forces that shaped reality itself, could not find it when it chose to be hidden.
Yet, there was always one who seemed to possess an unerring instinct for its location, a beacon in the vast, formless void of existence.
That being was THE Living Emotive.
One day, THE Creature had transformed itself into an Inevitability- a writhing mass of contradictions, pure hunger given form...to learn more of its kind.
As it drifted through a sea of unformed possibilities, a presence settled on its shoulder.
A being of pure emotion, a flicker of light in the maelstrom of its hungry form.
THE Creature, recognizing the signature, sighed with an exasperation that seemed to shake the very concepts of anger and annoyance.
"How do you always manage to find me?" THE Creature's thought resonated, a question not of power, but of genuine curiosity.
"You are an enigma, a weaving of power and potential that defies all understanding," THE Living Emotive replied, its voice a melody of feelings, each note a different emotion.
"You can hide your form, mask your power, and even obscure your consciousness from the others. But your emotions... your emotions, O Creature, will always be something you can never hide from me."

|Your Necromancy and Death Towers of Osmont burn with power and recognition, their aid, along with Cheats and all other Vital Lighthouses of the Early Atlas of the Folds, have brought about an unprecedented result.|
| As of this moment, your Legion of Dead Existences has gained its first member.|
Noah's eyes on the prompts were a silent, incandescent flash of triumph.
The Seed of Perpetual Harvest had rewarded his effort, his tyrannical will, by allowing him to harvest a life not of his own, to command a being of death and hunger.
The fusion of his will with Ozymandias's hunger, and the raw authority of the ape's corpse, had created something that should not exist!
A Legion of Dead Existences, and this creature was its first member.
He would not be defined by the rules of Existence; he would bend them to his will!
The prompts continued to cascade, each one a testament to his growing power.
|The Dead Existential Inevitability, Primordial Stone Ape, has officially been born.|
|Primordial Stone Ape(Dead Existential Inevitability)|
|Complexity: 200,000,000,000,000 (200 Trillion)|
|Purity: 0 (All converted to Complexity to fuel its necrotic state)|
|Distinctions:|
|The Dead- A state of existence that defies cessation.
The creature will reform even if its weavings are completely collapsed.|
|Inevitability- The hunger of existence made manifest.
It devours and grows, fueled by any existence it consumes.|
|Necrotic Inevitability- A unique fusion of hunger and death.
It can consume both life and death, converting all matter and essence into its own power.|
|Early Butcher- A title inherited from Ozymandias, now an innate skill.
It can dissect any being of immense power with a terrifying efficiency.|
Noah's eyes, burning with a cold, tyrannical light, landed on the Primordial Stone Ape.
A single act of a being he hadn't even met, an act of sheer curiosity, had reduced him to a state of burning agony.
But now, that act, that curse, had been devoured and in its place, he had created something that would shake the very foundations of his current existence!
The ape began to move, its body shifting with a grace that seemed both dead and alive.
Its eyes, which had once held the terrifying will of Ozymandias, blinked.
And then, as if a veil had been lifted, it gained a return of its own sense of cognizance.
The terrifying power of The Dead flowed through it, an aura of utter regal darkness.

The countless tentacles of Ozymandias left the ape's body, and yet, brand new tentacles, formed of obsidian Early Dead Existential Authority, sprouted forth, weaving themselves into a terrifying new form.
The ape's lower body, once a mass of tentacles, became more and more real, its form now a brilliant obsidian-gold, with fur-like qualities that emanated profound waves of death.
It was a beautiful, horrifying creation, a perfect synthesis of life and death, of life and inevitability.
Ozymandias floated beside Noah, the two bodies standing side by side, a terrifying mirror of tyrannical power.
They looked upon this unique Dead Existence they had brought to fruition.
And in that moment, the ape, filled with the new cognizance of a being born of death and hunger, knelt.
Its massive hand rose to its chest and tapped three times, a greeting given to Early Creatures.
A gesture of submission and respect from a being of unfathomable power, a testament to the might of The Early Creature, Osmont!
On this day, Noah, for the first time, received the greeting given to Early Creatures from a Dead Existence that he had brought to fruition.
It was a victory born of suffering, a triumph forged in the fires of a curse!
Suffering.
A unique idea that seemed always present, but it became moreso at a point in time in distant past.
In the Earliest Folds, where the glorious potential of existence swirled and coalesced into form, a time existed when THE Creature's power grew so immense that its presence became a choice.
Even THE Living Existences, those who wielded the fundamental forces that shaped reality itself, could not find it when it chose to be hidden.
Yet, there was always one who seemed to possess an unerring instinct for its location, a beacon in the vast, formless void of existence.
That being was THE Living Emotive.
One day, THE Creature had transformed itself into an Inevitability- a writhing mass of contradictions, pure hunger given form...to learn more of its kind.
As it drifted through a sea of unformed possibilities, a presence settled on its shoulder.
A being of pure emotion, a flicker of light in the maelstrom of its hungry form.
THE Creature, recognizing the signature, sighed with an exasperation that seemed to shake the very concepts of anger and annoyance.
"How do you always manage to find me?" THE Creature's thought resonated, a question not of power, but of genuine curiosity.
"You are an enigma, a weaving of power and potential that defies all understanding," THE Living Emotive replied, its voice a melody of feelings, each note a different emotion.
"You can hide your form, mask your power, and even obscure your consciousness from the others.
But your emotions... your emotions, O Creature, will always be something you can never hide from me."

chapters.title: Chapter 4138 Hunger and Suffering! IV
paragraphs: As Emotive spoke, its form, which usually shifted through a spectrum of vibrant feelings, was now covered in a murky, roiling light of unhappiness and a nascent, terrifying rage.
THE Creature's eyes, a reflection of everything and nothing, were silent, observing the storm brewing within Emotive's being.

THE Living Emotive continued, its voice now laced with a philosophical gravitas. "I have spent eons observing, and I believe I have found the two great forces that drive existence: fear and love. Across all the Folds, in every life and every weaving, countless beings are driven by these two."

" Fear, because it is the most primal of emotions. It causes a hunter to rise each day, to seek sustenance, to build a home, all for the fear of being poor, or hungry, or alone. Fear of having no say in one's life, of being a slave to the will of others, a leaf caught in a storm"

"And love... ah, love is the counterbalance. It drives a being to find its counterpart, someone who understands them, feels their needs, and caters to them. In the pursuit of this love, empires are formed, countless complex weavings bloom, and beings rise to unimaginable heights."
THE Creature listened, its form shifting, a subtle nod of agreement in its posture.

"That is accurate," its voice resonated. "But others would say it is recognition and power that move existence. They seek to leave a mark, to not be insignificant. They desire to have a voice, to command and be obeyed. You, my dear Emotive, are yourself driven by this need for recognition, and I fear it may just destroy you... or countless others."
THE Creature's form, an Inevitability of pure hunger, shifted. "I know the others have not been kind to you. But whatever it is you are planning... turn back. Do not do it."
THE Creature's warning was not a command, but a plea. It was the first, and perhaps only, to see that THE Living Emotive had reached a tipping point, a place of no return.
But at that moment, THE Living Emotive could only smile. It was a chilling emotion, a light that burned with a terrifying, unholy fire.
It was a smile that spoke of a point of no return, of a plan already set in motion.
"There is no turning back," THE Living Emotive's voice whispered, a promise of impending doom.
It paused, its form roiling with a tumultuous array of feelings, and then a cold, frightening light replaced all other emotions.
"Actually," it said, "I will change my answer. The biggest drive for existence... is suffering. A powerful emotion. A powerful state. Through suffering, many will find their drive in existence."

"Through suffering, beings discover their true nature. Through suffering, they find meaning in meaninglessness. A comfortable existence teaches nothing, but suffering? Suffering transforms. A child who never knows hunger never appreciates food. A being who never faces loss never values what they have. Suffering is the greatest teacher, the most honest friend, the only force that creates genuine growth."
BOOM!
Its voice carried the weight of decision already made.

"So let there be endless suffering. Let every existence know pain intimate enough to transform them. Let comfort become memory and struggle become constant. Through this gift of suffering, existence will finally achieve its potential...not through gentle guidance but through desperate necessity."

THE Creature felt Existence shift slightly, reality accepting a new constant that shouldn't have been possible to implement. THE Living Emotive had done something fundamental, something that couldn't be reversed.
"What have you done?" THE Creature asked, though it already knew.

"I've given existence what it needs but doesn't want. I've ensured that suffering will find everyone, Everything, eventually. Not cruelly...lovingly. As a parent who knows their child needs hardship to grow strong."
THE Living Emotive departed then, leaving THE Creature alone with the knowledge that existence had just become infinitely harder for every being that would ever be.

The weavings of guaranteed suffering had begun, implemented by the one Living Existence whose nature meant it would feel every bit of that suffering infinitely more intensely than those who experienced it.
Perhaps that was the point.
Perhaps THE Living Emotive had chosen the ultimate form of recognition...becoming the source of the force that would shape all existence forever after!
Suffering, more often than not, was followed by glory.
In the Early Veiled Shore, brilliant waves of glory permeated the air, a testament to Noah's rapid ascension!
In a short period of mere days, he had gone from a Primarch to a Duke, his power now measured in trillions of Complexity and Purity.

The True Sources he had once held, mere concepts when he was moving in the Nullvein Gravewake Folds, were now composed of countless Dimensional Lattices, the foundation of his unshakeable Towers of Osmont.
Among these, the True Sources of Necromancy and Death burned with power at this particular time due to their recent achievement of the Primordial Stone Ape!
But like all things, they had their beginnings.
And when it came to necromancy and death, Noah also had his beginnings.
At this moment, Noah gazed at the glorious visage of the Primordial Stone Ape, its body now a grotesque but magnificent fusion of flesh, bone, and hunger.
The ape, sitting at a staggering 200 Trillion Complexity, seemed to be undergoing a unique metamorphosis.
Its obsidian-gold eyes now shone with a nascent intelligence, an intelligence born of the Early Dead Existential Authority coursing through its veins.
The authority was not of the living, nor was it the raging, primordial energy of the Earliest Folds.
It was a silent, obsidian dread!
The air around the ape felt heavy, stifling, and across the Shore, some beings felt its oppressive gaze as it looked around!
The Blue Slime, a being of pure chaos and carefree demeanor, instinctively hid behind the Emperor Penguin, its gelatinous form trembling.
Even though the ape meant no harm, its very existence was an oppressive weight!
Titano and others stared forth with amazement as they wondered what all of this would lead to!

chapters.title: Chapter 4139 Collective Ascendancy! I
paragraphs: Noah released a breath of tyranny, a level of calm settling over him after the chaotic events of the day.
In the next moment, a buzzing sensation coursed through the depths of his existence, and a prompt rose to meet his eye.
|The Weavings of the Protagonist remembers the one who led your Legions of Undead, and feels nostalgic as its weavings are calling out Arch Lich Ra'Zan.|
The Arch Lich, Ra'Zan.
A slight smile, a ghost of a long-forgotten memory, touched Noah's lips. A sense of nostalgia, a wave of remembrance for the journey of the last three years, washed over him.
He thought of his earlier Skill Trees, how a poisonous Abomination had, through his will, been refined into an Arch Lich.

He remembered its overpowered skills, the Unstable Necrotic Ring of Death, a spiraling storm of bones and death that had decimated his foes. He had elevated the Arch Lich skill tree and many others, refined it until it became a Reified ability and much more...a testament to his journey!
The thought of all this, of the glorious ways he had expressed authority over the years, took him back to the very beginning.
The Fireball skill, the Arch Lich- these were the foundations of his being, of his empire.
He closed his eyes, a silent nod of permission given to the Weavings of the Protagonist, and the Shore held its breath!
A moment later, the massive body of the Primordial Stone Ape began to tremble, as if something was trying to rise from within it.

|For the record of the Arch Lich Ra'Zan to be brought back to fruition, and even granted the distinction of a Dead Existence and Dead Existential Inevitability is unfathomably hard. The Dead are rare, and even moreso with the distinction of Inevitability.|
| To allow for its success at this moment, it would have to come from the complexity of the Primordial Stone Ape itself.|
|50 Trillion of its complexity would be required to allow for the undertaking you desire, proceed?|
The prompt asked him, and Noah smiled.
A price of 50 Trillion for a being he had not seen in months, a being that he himself had refined and designed. It was a price he would gladly pay. He nodded, and the Shore responded.
The glorious scene was a blend of life and death, of glory and sacrifice!
HUUM!
The ape's chest, still a grotesque mosaic of flesh and tentacles, split open. The ape blinked and looked down with a curious gaze as an obsidian-gold light of death and bones began to form.
The process was meticulous, a meticulous reconstruction of a long-forgotten being!
Bones were assembled, one by one, each piece shining with a brilliant, dark light, followed by an obsidian-gold robe.
In the end, an elevated version of a Lich appeared, its skeletal form a terrifying testament to Noah's power.
The Lich's bones shone with an obsidian-gold radiance, its robe a shimmering weaving of death!

Early Dead Existential Authority swirled around it, a dense, palpable force that bowed to its will. In its hands, a crystalline bony staff with an obsidian-gold crystal was clutched, a weapon that hummed with a silent, terrifying power.
Prompts bloomed, their words a grand proclamation of this new, yet old, design!

|The Arch Lich, Ra'Zan, had its record refined and brought out again as a Dead Existential Inevitability. This is a glorious achievement of sacrifice and effort. Due to the nature of the Arch Lich being capable of summoning undead lifeforms, this action has shockingly paved the way for Dead Existences to now be capable of being summoned through the Arch Lich. The distinction of a Dead Existential Inevitability is a title held only by The Arch Lich Ra'Zan and the Primordial Stone Ape.|
|The complexity of the Primordial Stone Ape has been reduced to 150 Trillion in order to pave way for the Arch Lich Ra'Zan.|
|The Arch Lich...pays respect to its Master.|
BOOM!
Waves of obsidian gold authority raged!
An instant later, the newly formed Arch Lich floated toward Noah.
The chest of the Primordial Stone Ape closed, and Ra'Zan, a king of death, knelt before Noah, his bony head bowing in a gesture of profound fealty.
Glorious, Quintessential fealty!
His words, a glorious, deathly sound, echoed in the silent Shore.
"This servant is beyond happy to be called to serve again."
WAA!
Noah gazed at the Arch Lich, a smile gracing his lips. The journey from a simple skill to a Dead Existential Inevitability was a glorious, unbelievable weaving of reality.
From a simple Abomination, all the way to not just a Dead Existence, but a Dead Existential Inevitability!
Oh!
He touched the vibrant skeletal head of the Arch Lich, and a status sheet bloomed before his eyes.
|ARCH LICH RA'ZAN - THE NECROTIC ARCHITECT|
|Complexity: 50,000,000,000,000 (+50 Trillion)|
|Purity: 0 (Converted to Complexity to fuel his necrotic state)|
|Distinctions:|
|The Dead- A state of existence that defies cessation. The creature will reform even if its weavings are completely collapsed.|
|Inevitability- The hunger of existence made manifest. It devours and grows, fueled by any existence it consumes.|
|Necrotic Architect- A distinction unique to Ra'Zan. He can summon dead lifeforms, imbuing them with the Authority of The Dead and a portion of his own power.|
|Inherent Skills:|

|Summon The Dead- Allows for the summoning of Dead Existences, not Inevitabilities, which can be commanded to do his bidding. The complexity of these summons is a fraction of his own, but they have the possibility of advancement as he advances|

|Inevitable Fold Ring of Death- A constantly swirling ring of death, filled with the essence of all of Ra'Zan's distinctions, that can be cast upon a Fold. The ring tears and devours all matter and essence within it, reducing them to nothingness. The more powerful the ring, the greater the Fold it can devour.|
Noah's eyes burned with glory as he viewed the terrifying status sheet of Ra'Zan with a mind that saw not just power, but potential.
A single being, a mere concept, could now summon Dead Existences, a force that would bow to his will!
The possibilities were endless.
Because what was currently the main issue to be discussed at the Kleos Concordat?!
Was it not...Dead Existences?!
"Haha..." Noah couldn't help but laugh for the first time since the threat of death.
And beside him...
"KaKaKa!" An Arch Lich laughed alongside its Master, its eyes a swirl of madness and death!
