chapters.title: Chapter 4172 Progression! I
paragraphs: In the Transcendent Temporal Folds, beneath the ever-expanding canopy of the Tree of Unity, Noah watched Schrodinger's retreating figure with eyes that processed information on multiple levels simultaneously.

The beggar-paradox moved through the crowd with that particular gait of someone who had just confirmed something important, though what that something might be remained locked behind his perpetual smile.
Beside Noah, Khor shifted slightly, and when she spoke, it wasn't with her voice but directly into his consciousness...a private communication that bypassed sound entirely.

'In the olden times,' her mental voice carried weight that suggested firsthand memory rather than historical knowledge, 'when it had gotten to the point where Early Creatures were unruly and spreading chaos and decimation across the Earliest Folds, THE Living Law had sought a weapon in order to keep them under control.'
Noah's attention sharpened, though his expression remained unchanged.
Around them, the amphitheater buzzed with discussions of unity and cooperation, but this private revelation cast everything in a different light.

'I may be wrong,' Khor continued, though her tone suggested she rarely was, 'but based on what I remember, the tiny leaf that the existence you call Schrodinger pulled out should possibly be a part of that weapon that was utilized by THE Living Law at that time.'
HUUM!
She turned to face him directly then, her ancient eyes containing depths that had seen the rise and fall of concepts themselves.

'Though, what is even more astounding is the fact that a weapon that is highly effective against Early Creatures was pulled out against you, and yet, you did not even falter or sense anything.' A pause, heavy with implication. 'Outsider, you... are an Early Creature, right?'
The question hung between them with daring that transcended simple inquiry. It was the kind of question that could reshape understanding of everything!
Noah's mind raced through the implications with the speed of someone who had long ago learned that survival often depended on understanding what others truly wanted before they knew it themselves.
Schrodinger had pulled out that leaf specifically because he believed Noah was an Early Creature. It had been a test...elegant in its simplicity, terrifying in its implications.
The leaf hadn't worked.

Which meant Schrodinger now faced two possible conclusions: either Noah wasn't an Early Creature at all, which would overturn numerous assumptions about his nature and power, or- and this was the more disturbing possibility, Noah was indeed an Early Creature, but one against whom traditional weapons simply didn't function.
The question that naturally followed made Noah's thoughts spiral into deeper analysis. Why exactly would a weapon utilized and effective against Early Creatures not work against him?
He possessed astounding concepts, certainly.

The Protagonist, Cheats, Tyranny, and others that defied conventional understanding. But at the end of the day, Noah knew who he was...or at least, he thought he did. He didn't consider himself unfathomably special, despite evidence increasingly suggesting otherwise.
The only theoretical difference he could identify was in the fundamental structure of his existence compared to other Early Creatures!

He wasn't simply an Early Creature...he was The Early Creature, Osmont. Part of him was also an Inevitability, a hybrid nature that shouldn't exist. His progression of power followed patterns drastically different from any Early Creature recorded in history.
None of them held the Towers of Osmont that rose within his being like monuments to impossible achievement!
None possessed the Early Atlas of the Folds that provided pathways to temporal traversal of the Earliest Folds themselves.
His very physiology, his way of existing, was fundamentally distinct from traditional Early Creatures.
But he couldn't say with certainty which aspect had rendered him immune to the leaf's effects. Was it his hybrid nature? The Towers? The Atlas? His Infinite Mana? Or perhaps something else entirely?
He filed these questions away for future contemplation as more immediate matters demanded attention.

Returning to where Sigrid stood, he found her wearing an expression of barely contained annoyance while Beast Shepherdess Miki bounced enthusiastically nearby, Fluffy's massive form creating its own gravitational field of terror and oddly endearing loyalty.

"Beast Shepherdess Miki here," Sigrid said with the particular tone of someone delivering a report they found personally irritating, "and her supposedly sweet Spirit Beast Fluffy seem to want to bask in the light of Order. Fluffy is apparently cursed with rage, and my authority helped calm it earlier."
Noah raised his eyebrows at this, glancing at the enthusiastic Miki who was practically vibrating with excitement.

Her smile could have powered small civilizations with its brightness. He shook his head slightly, then looked up at the radiant Tree of Unity that continued to grow with each new contribution of authority.
A decisive light flashed in his eyes as he made a choice that would ripple through the gathering.
His voice rang out with clarity that cut through the ambient conversations.
"We shall reinforce the forces in the Wandering Territories against The Dead."
WAA!
The declaration landed with weight that made numerous beings turn their attention toward him.
He wanted to expand his field of knowledge, certainly, but more than that, the sanctuary of The First Farmer hidden in the Wandering Territories was of great interest to him.

This was the entity who had, through whatever chain of causality, provided him with the Failed Seed that had become the Principle of Perpetual Harvest. Understanding that connection felt crucial to understanding himself.
His words created a cascade effect!
Origin Ama Gias, not to be outdone and allow THE Living Order to slip past her, raised her voice with authority that made space itself stand at attention.
"The Living Origins shall also reinforce the Wandering Territories. We will not allow The Dead to gain foothold there."
Beast Shepherdess Miki practically exploded with enthusiasm. "Oh yes! Yes! Fluffy and I will definitely help! The Wandering Territories sound amazing! Plus, Fluffy needs more meat, don't you, boy?"
She patted the quadrillion-complexity beast like it was a regular dog, which somehow made the scene more terrifying rather than less.
Melancholic Sovereign Drai rose with his characteristic aura of depression that made nearby beings unconsciously slouch.
"Since we're all going to die eventually anyway, might as well die together in the Wandering Territories. At leastm... the scenery might be different before the inevitable end."
His words were fucking depressive!
Among the Living Paradoxes, a more subtle exchange was taking place.
Schrodinger had sidled up to the massive form of Goliath, whose serpentine body redefined the local geography simply by existing.

"Hey, scary guy," Schrodinger said with casual familiarity that would have been suicidal from anyone else, "you might benefit more to send one of your bodies over to the Wandering Territories. Many more exquisite things to eat there, and you could keep an eye on that... Osmontian for me."
Goliath didn't even turn to acknowledge Schrodinger, his voice emerging from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously.
"Do not cause too much chaos. Otherwise, you will add me to your list of enemies."

Many more exquisite things to eat there, and you could keep an eye on that...
Osmontian for me."
Goliath didn't even turn to acknowledge Schrodinger, his voice emerging from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously.
"Do not cause too much chaos.
Otherwise, you will add me to your list of enemies."

chapters.title: Chapter 4173 Progression! II
paragraphs: The threat was delivered with such certainty that several nearby Paradoxes actually stepped back. Schrodinger only smiled and nodded, then turned his attention upward.
"O Powerful Fold Dwellers," he called out with theatrical humility, "us Living Paradoxes are weak, but we will have one of our most steadfast soldiers, Goliath, join in to support with a few others!"
Elysia Firmhand gazed down with eyes that could have frozen concepts. Her response came with the weight of someone who had already calculated every possible outcome.
"For those coming to reinforce the Wandering Territories, we leave in five. Make your decisions by that time." She gestured to her twin beside her.
"My brother, Caelum Firmhand of the Blue Fields, will stay here with others to coordinate any movements for Living Existences across the Folds."
Caelum nodded, his rake shifting in his grip with movement that suggested entire harvests being planned.
"This time when The Dead are not prevalent and barely any Tears of Existence have opened," Elysia continued, "will be the most critical!"
The stage was set.
Noah's eyes burned with possibilities as the Kleos Concordat had led to unexpected results and meetings, but he would keep moving forward with his own preparations.
The game had become more complex, the players more numerous, but the goal remained the same...survival and transcendence, in whatever order proved necessary.
Behind him, a voice filled with indignation broke through his thoughts.
"Master, we didn't even get to show off!"

The Emperor Penguin raised his beak with pride that seemed personally offended by the lack of combat. Noah smiled while patting the bird's head, the gesture both affectionate and condescending in the way that only Emperor Penguin seemed to appreciate.

He looked at Kazuhiko, whose hand rested on his sword with the patience of someone who knew violence was inevitable. Erikson stood in his beach attire, the Slipper of Existential Humiliation tucked casually in his waistband. The Queen of Matter had already begun documenting everything in one of her floating books.
"You'll get to play soon enough," Noah assured them. "Come, let us finish preparations."
He turned to Khor, and her eyes lit up with anticipation that made reality nervous.
"Is it that time, Outsider?"
Is it that time?
The unspoken completion of the question hung in the air as truly...it was time to swallow an entire Fold!
The casual impossibility of it, stated as if discussing lunch plans, made several nearby beings edge away despite not hearing the actual words.
Noah nodded, his authority wrapping around Khor with precision that had been refined through impossible practice.
In one moment she was there, in the next, she simply wasn't...transported to wherever Folds would be devoured!

Sigrid moved beside him with grace, Ruination and the Infiniverse flanking them as they all gazed up at the Fold Dwellers and the ever-growing Tree of Unity. The sight was magnificent in its implications...forced cooperation on a scale that existence had never before witnessed.
Noah's expression grew cold with solemnity that made the temperature around him drop as he looked ahead.
Sigrid, sensitive to his moods, asked quietly, "What is it?"
He turned to her, and his words carried weight that made her straighten instinctively.
"We will have to send one of your bodies to the Transcendent Origin Folds. It seems soon, a catastrophe is coming to it. It should be a good place to cultivate your Order."
WAA!
The words landed with the force of prophecy.

Sigrid nodded without hesitation. Even though she had told the Living Origins she would not establish Order with them, even though she had rejected their authority and chosen her own path, that was still her home in ways that transcended politics or power.

The Living Origins were where she had learned what Origin meant, where her family had sacrificed everything for a concept that she now embodied in ways they never could have imagined. If chaos was coming to that place, she would be there for it!
Not for them, but for what they had once represented. For the memory of her Ama who had taught her to guide without controlling.
For the echo of possibilities that had been sacrificed on Order's altar.
"I'll go," she said simply, the words carrying certainty that made them more than agreement...they were declaration, promise, and threat combined.

Noah nodded, already calculating deployments, contingencies, and the very real possibility that Schrodinger's warnings about the Origin Folds weren't warnings at all, but promises of chaos he had orchestrated himself.
The only question was for what purpose?
The gathering was dispersing with purpose now, each faction preparing for movements that would reshape the Folds against The Dead.

But Noah couldn't shake the feeling that the real game was being played on a board none of them could fully see, with pieces that didn't know they were pieces, toward an ending that might not be an ending at all.
Above them, the Tree of Unity continued to grow, its roots spreading through dimensions that didn't have names, its branches reaching toward futures that hadn't decided whether to exist!

In Aeternitas Concordia, deep within the golden streets of the marketplace where weak Fold Dwellers haggled alongside beings who could unmake reality with a thought, Noah sat upon a radiant throne that he had manifested from pure authority!
The morning's trade had been particularly profitable...not in terms of resources gained, though those were substantial, but in information gathered.
"Alright, that's all the trading for now!"
His voice carried across the marketplace with finality that brooked no argument.

With practiced motions, he began storing away the Glass Woks and bowls that had contained the meat of Marine Lifeforms from his Early Veiled Shore...delicacies that beings here couldn't obtain through any other means.
The crowd that had gathered, a mixture of hopeful Fold Dwellers and calculating Living Existences, began to disperse with varying degrees of reluctance.
Beside him, Kalysta and the other Fold Dwellers from the Veiled Sunfolds remained, their expressions mixing gratitude with confusion at the sudden end to commerce.
Noah turned to them, his gaze carrying weight that made even these beings who had grown accustomed to his strangeness pay attention.
"You all need to go now."
Kalysta's eyes flashed with kismet, that particular light that suggested she was seeing fragments of possibility.
Her mouth opened to reply, perhaps to question. But before sound could emerge, Noah's hand moved with certainty.
White-gold light erupted from his gesture with the patient inevitability of sunrise.

It wrapped around Kalysta, the Originus Venerant entities, and every being connected to the Veiled Sunfolds. The light didn't transport them so much as exchange them, reality shuffling its deck to deal a different hand.
Where they had stood, a single figure now materialized.
Sigrid's clone appeared with the grace of Order asserting itself in a space that had momentarily forgotten structure!
THE Living Order returned...to her home!

chapters.title: Chapter 4174 You called them! I
paragraphs: Her dark and white hair fell in waves that seemed to exist in perfect symmetry, each strand knowing exactly where it belonged!
The white robe she wore was authority given form.
Her eyes lit with complex recognition as she looked around, taking in the familiar-yet-different architecture of this nexus where all Living Existences mingled.
Then her gaze rose higher, piercing through dimensional barriers with the ease of someone looking through clear glass.
She stared across the vast expanse of the Transcendent Origin Folds, her attention fixing on a distant point that pulled at her with gravity that transcended the physical.
The Heart of Origin.
Her home.
The word carried weight that nearly made her falter!
Home...where her family had burned themselves to ash for the sake of Order.
Home, where every corner held memories of laughter before it held memories of sacrifice.
Home, where she had learned what love meant by watching it destroy itself for principle.
She moved to stand beside Noah, her voice emerging with melancholy that made the golden air around them grow heavy.

"I miss the memories of that place and what it used to represent," she said, each word carefully chosen yet with emotion. "But I hate the people there. The Royal Living Origins who made that choice. The Dukes who convinced my Ama that sacrifice was the only path. The ones who watched my family burn and called it necessity."
Her eyes carried traces of longing mixed with pain...the particular anguish of loving a place while hating what it had become!
The moment Noah saw that expression, his eyes sharpened to points that could have cut through the veils between realities.
"I could decimate all those Living Origins that caused you pain."
The offer was delivered with the same tone someone might use to suggest getting dinner.
Casual. Certain. Absolutely sincere.
Sigrid's lips curved into a smile that contained too much understanding to be happy.
She shook her head, preparing to explain why vengeance wouldn't heal what had been broken, but-
HUUM!
The sound rolled across existence like thunder from a storm that hadn't formed yet. It wasn't loud so much as deep, resonating in frequencies that bones recognized before ears could process.
Noah and Sigrid looked up simultaneously, their enhanced perceptions cutting through dimensional layers to see what was coming.
Across the vast stretches of the Transcendent Origin Folds, there had only been auroras of beautiful white and gold...the natural luminescence of Origin authority permeating through structured space.
Yet at this moment, from all directions at once...
WU! WU! WU!
Hues of obsidian began blooming in the far distance like inverse stars igniting.

The light was wrong in ways that transcended color...it felt grand and terrible, as if it were leaking from a place that should have been sealed, as if death that had been carefully contained had suddenly found its dams exploding.
RIIP!
Space began to tear. Not in one location but across different regions throughout the Transcendent Origin Folds!

The tears started as lines of absolute black against reality's fabric, then widened into oval doorways that spilled endless weavings of death and endings. Each tear was perfectly positioned, surgically precise in its placement...too precise to be natural, too coordinated to be coincidence.
The marketplace erupted into chaos as Living Existences recognized the threat.
Above Concordia, multiple auras of Duke-level power blazed to life like defensive fires against approaching winter.
These weren't just Living Origin Dukes...the Coalition of Living Existences had members here from every faction here, and they all responded with trained precision to existential threat!

Tens of thousands of Royal, Honored, and Prime Living Existences began gathering with speed that bent space around their movement. They looked at the widening tears with expressions that cycled through shock, fear, and a desperate question that none wanted to voice- Why?
They had received no reports of mass tears opening in other Transcendent Folds.
So why was it that so many tears were opening specifically in the Transcendent Origin Folds?
Noah's eyes remained sharp as he observed the swathes of Living Existences scrambling to respond.
He understood what they didn't...when one lacked the right knowledge, they could only ever move reactively, playing a game whose rules they didn't know existed.
These beings saw the Tears of Existence and thought simply: The Dead will emerge and cause destruction if not stopped.
They didn't know, couldn't know, that these tears were likely purposeful, deliberate, orchestrated!
They didn't understand that existence itself didn't have particular animosity toward the Transcendent Origin Folds. This wasn't existential judgment but collateral damage in someone else's plan.
The machinations of Schrodinger, most likely. A paradox needing something from here, and willing to sacrifice an entire Fold's stability to obtsin his means!
None of them knew this. But Noah held more information than most, could do more than simply react to unfolding catastrophe. He could prepare. He could plan. He could profit.
At this moment, Noah had a very specific goal: One Quadrillion.
He had become a Duke. Exceeded ten trillion in complexity and purity. By most measures, this was magnificent achievement.
But so what?
Young Early Creatures...not even mature ones, but their young, were born with one quadrillion.
One thousand trillion as their starting point!
How could he be satisfied with a mere ten trillion when he was supposed to be an Early Creature? When he bore the title of The Early Creature, Osmont?!
The disparity gnawed at him with mathematics that demanded resolution.
He needed to bridge that gap not gradually but exponentially. He needed resources, opportunities, and challenges that would force his evolution beyond current limitations!
HUUM!
His eyes pulsed with bursts of blue-gold arcs that formed infinity symbols in the air before dissolving.
His gaze rose to focus on the Tears of Existence with the particular attention of a farmer examining fields ready for harvest.
Whatever came through those tears, he would break down and devour to aid his elevation toward one quadrillion!
Let them come. Let them all come!
His body began to vibrate with anticipation that transcended the physical. His existence itself buzzed with fervor, resonating at frequencies that made nearby space reconsider its stability!
Prompts materialized before his vision:
|Your existence senses weavings of unfathomable danger and opportunity approaching|
|The Seed of the Principle of Perpetual Harvest recognizes the effort you wish to exert|
|Analyzing optimal support configuration...|
|The Principle of Perpetual Harvest throws its support wholly toward: Your Weavings of Loot|
|Loot probability increased by 1000%|
|Loot quality increased by 1000%|
|All enemies defeated will drop maximum possible resources|
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4175 You called them! II
paragraphs: Golden arcs of loot light erupted across Noah's body, wreathing him in radiance that suggested wealth about to be forcibly extracted from reality!
His eyes pulsed with glory that made several nearby beings step back instinctively.
He rose from his throne with movement that was both gradual and instantaneous, existing in the space between rest and violence.
His heart...the Heart of an Early Creature that beat within his chest, began pounding like a war drum announcing the beginning of harvest!
The sound resonated through dimensions, each beat a promise of violence transformed into opportunity. He opened his mouth, and what emerged wasn't quite a word but pure expression of desire!
"COME!"
HUUM!
The howl boomed across the Transcendent Origin Folds like a glorious commandment.
Every Duke in the vicinity turned toward him with expressions of incredulous horror. What did he mean, come?!
Did this madman actually want whatever lurked behind those tears to emerge?
This fucker!
As if responding to his invitation, change erupted from the largest tear directly above Concordia.
A massive mummified head emerged first, wearing a golden crown that had tarnished with age that predated the proper invention of time.

The skull was wrapped in bandages that might have once been white but had yellowed and blackened with accumulated death. Eye sockets that should have been empty blazed with unholy light that made existence itself want to look away!
Mummified hands followed, each finger the size of a building's foundation, moving with speed that large things shouldn't possess.
They grasped the edges of the tear and pulled, ripping reality wider with the casual strength of something that had been waiting too long to be gentle!
The full creature that emerged made several Dukes actually pale...a physical response that beings of their level shouldn't have been capable of experiencing.
Noah's enhanced perception immediately began calculating, measuring the waves of power that radiated from this first arrival.
Five hundred trillion. At minimum!
Fuck!
The first Dead Existence to fully emerge already eclipsed many of the assembled Dukes in raw power.
Its presence pressed against reality with weight that made lesser beings simply cease, not from attack but from proximity to something that shouldn't exist.
Across the Transcendent Origin Folds, the tears continued disgorging their contents.
Eidolons emerged...beings of pure death-force that had forgotten they once had bodies.
Wights crawled through, their forms constantly shifting between what they had been and what death had made them.
Each tear revealed new horrors, new impossibilities, new opportunities for those brave or foolish enough to seize them.
Then, from one particular tear that seemed deeper than the others, something different emerged.
A winged head poked through first...not attached to a body but floating independently, supported by wings that had too many joints and moved in directions that space didn't normally permit.
Tentacles surrounded it like a living crown, each one tipped with eyes that saw in spectrums existence hadn't named.
Noah's gloriously burning figure was forced to focus on this particular emergence because from it, he felt something that made his blood sing with recognition and challenge!
The aura of an Early Creature!
Among The Dead, a Winged Head of an Early Creature had actually spilled across The Veil!
Not a Duke, not a mere powerful existence, but something that had walked in the Earliest Folds before walking became a concept that needed definition.
Oh!
The exclamation escaped him as pure expression of delighted recognition.
This wasn't catastrophe!
This was opportunity wearing catastrophe's mask!
This was Existence delivering exactly what he needed, wrapped in packaging that would terrify anyone sensible enough to refuse the gift.
The Dead had come in force, and among them, something worth devouring.
The overflowing aura of The Dead pressed against reality with weight that made existence reconsider its structural integrity!
Noah gazed at the unfolding catastrophe with eyes that shone with both gravity and possibility...the particular gleam of someone doing math that would horrify accountants.
Twenty trillion in complexity and purity. It was nice, certainly.
The kind of power that could reshape Folds, that made him a Duke among weaker Dukes.

But when faced with Dead Existences measuring in the hundreds of trillions, when an Early Creature's winged head was emerging with power approaching a single quadrillion markers... it wasn't entirely up to the task.
But he wasn't alone. He had another body...Ozymandias, whose purity had been refined to impossible heights! And he had something else, something that most here couldn't imagine.
A Legion of The Dead himself.
The masses of Aeternitas Concordia had gone pale...an achievement for beings whose complexions ranged from crystalline to void-touched.
Many turned toward Noah with expressions of expectant anticipation in their fear.
He had bellowed "COME!" with such magnificent authority.
Surely now he would charge forward, leading the defense against these monstrosities?
Noah met their gazes without changing expression.
Then, with the casual certainty of someone who had just remembered he'd left something behind, he floated back down beside Sigrid.
He settled into a comfortable hovering position with his arms crossed, wearing the particular expression of someone waiting for a show to begin!
The silence that followed was deafening.
"What in the collapsed Folds are you doing?!" a Duke of Living Origins actually shouted, dignity forgotten in confusion.
"You called them here!" accused another, pointing at the emerging horrors. "You literally invited them!"
Noah continued watching with polite interest, as if the accusations were happening in a language he didn't speak.

Sigrid beside him had to suppress her expression as she was also somber...she knew that expression, had seen it before when he was about to do something that would make everyone reassess their understanding of possibility.
What they didn't know, couldn't know, was that Noah wasn't retreating. He was simply allowing another part of himself to shine.
In the next moment, as terrifying Dead Existences began fully emerging from tears that shouldn't exist...
"Ka! Ka! Ka!"
The cackling cut through the chaos like a scythe through wheat.
From a blooming portal of obsidian light and bones that materialized with theatrical precision in the same above Concordia, Arch Lich Ra'Zan made his entrance!
His skeletal form was magnificent in its terrible glory...bones of obsidian-gold that caught light in ways that suggested they existed in more dimensions than were strictly necessary.
His skull blazed with green-gold flames that danced with genuine amusement. Tattered robes that seemed woven from the final breaths of dying Folds billowed around him despite the absence of wind!
He stood atop the emerging Primordial Stone Ape, whose undead form had grown even more terrifying since its transformation.
And leading them both, moving with the inexorable certainty of hunger given purpose...
Ozymandias!

sentences.text: Golden arcs of loot light erupted across Noah's body, wreathing him in radiance that suggested wealth about to be forcibly extracted from reality!
His eyes pulsed with glory that made several nearby beings step back instinctively.
He rose from his throne with movement that was both gradual and instantaneous, existing in the space between rest and violence.
His heart...the Heart of an Early Creature that beat within his chest, began pounding like a war drum announcing the beginning of harvest!
The sound resonated through dimensions, each beat a promise of violence transformed into opportunity.
He opened his mouth, and what emerged wasn't quite a word but pure expression of desire!
"COME!"
HUUM!
The howl boomed across the Transcendent Origin Folds like a glorious commandment.
Every Duke in the vicinity turned toward him with expressions of incredulous horror.
What did he mean, come?!
Did this madman actually want whatever lurked behind those tears to emerge?
This fucker!
As if responding to his invitation, change erupted from the largest tear directly above Concordia.
A massive mummified head emerged first, wearing a golden crown that had tarnished with age that predated the proper invention of time.
The skull was wrapped in bandages that might have once been white but had yellowed and blackened with accumulated death.
Eye sockets that should have been empty blazed with unholy light that made existence itself want to look away!
Mummified hands followed, each finger the size of a building's foundation, moving with speed that large things shouldn't possess.
They grasped the edges of the tear and pulled, ripping reality wider with the casual strength of something that had been waiting too long to be gentle!
The full creature that emerged made several Dukes actually pale...a physical response that beings of their level shouldn't have been capable of experiencing.
Noah's enhanced perception immediately began calculating, measuring the waves of power that radiated from this first arrival.
Five hundred trillion.
At minimum!
Fuck!
The first Dead Existence to fully emerge already eclipsed many of the assembled Dukes in raw power.
Its presence pressed against reality with weight that made lesser beings simply cease, not from attack but from proximity to something that shouldn't exist.
Across the Transcendent Origin Folds, the tears continued disgorging their contents.
Eidolons emerged...beings of pure death-force that had forgotten they once had bodies.
Wights crawled through, their forms constantly shifting between what they had been and what death had made them.
Each tear revealed new horrors, new impossibilities, new opportunities for those brave or foolish enough to seize them.
Then, from one particular tear that seemed deeper than the others, something different emerged.
A winged head poked through first...not attached to a body but floating independently, supported by wings that had too many joints and moved in directions that space didn't normally permit.
Tentacles surrounded it like a living crown, each one tipped with eyes that saw in spectrums existence hadn't named.
Noah's gloriously burning figure was forced to focus on this particular emergence because from it, he felt something that made his blood sing with recognition and challenge!
The aura of an Early Creature!
Among The Dead, a Winged Head of an Early Creature had actually spilled across The Veil!
Not a Duke, not a mere powerful existence, but something that had walked in the Earliest Folds before walking became a concept that needed definition.
Oh!
The exclamation escaped him as pure expression of delighted recognition.
This wasn't catastrophe!
This was opportunity wearing catastrophe's mask!
This was Existence delivering exactly what he needed, wrapped in packaging that would terrify anyone sensible enough to refuse the gift.
The Dead had come in force, and among them, something worth devouring.
The overflowing aura of The Dead pressed against reality with weight that made existence reconsider its structural integrity!
Noah gazed at the unfolding catastrophe with eyes that shone with both gravity and possibility...the particular gleam of someone doing math that would horrify accountants.
Twenty trillion in complexity and purity.
It was nice, certainly.
The kind of power that could reshape Folds, that made him a Duke among weaker Dukes.

But when faced with Dead Existences measuring in the hundreds of trillions, when an Early Creature's winged head was emerging with power approaching a single quadrillion markers... it wasn't entirely up to the task.
But he wasn't alone.
He had another body...Ozymandias, whose purity had been refined to impossible heights!
And he had something else, something that most here couldn't imagine.
A Legion of The Dead himself.
The masses of Aeternitas Concordia had gone pale...an achievement for beings whose complexions ranged from crystalline to void-touched.
Many turned toward Noah with expressions of expectant anticipation in their fear.
He had bellowed "COME!" with such magnificent authority.
Surely now he would charge forward, leading the defense against these monstrosities?
Noah met their gazes without changing expression.
Then, with the casual certainty of someone who had just remembered he'd left something behind, he floated back down beside Sigrid.
He settled into a comfortable hovering position with his arms crossed, wearing the particular expression of someone waiting for a show to begin!
The silence that followed was deafening.
"What in the collapsed Folds are you doing?!" a Duke of Living Origins actually shouted, dignity forgotten in confusion.
"You called them here!" accused another, pointing at the emerging horrors.
"You literally invited them!"
Noah continued watching with polite interest, as if the accusations were happening in a language he didn't speak.

Sigrid beside him had to suppress her expression as she was also somber...she knew that expression, had seen it before when he was about to do something that would make everyone reassess their understanding of possibility.
What they didn't know, couldn't know, was that Noah wasn't retreating.
He was simply allowing another part of himself to shine.
In the next moment, as terrifying Dead Existences began fully emerging from tears that shouldn't exist...
"Ka!
Ka!
Ka!"
The cackling cut through the chaos like a scythe through wheat.
From a blooming portal of obsidian light and bones that materialized with theatrical precision in the same above Concordia, Arch Lich Ra'Zan made his entrance!
His skeletal form was magnificent in its terrible glory...bones of obsidian-gold that caught light in ways that suggested they existed in more dimensions than were strictly necessary.
His skull blazed with green-gold flames that danced with genuine amusement.
Tattered robes that seemed woven from the final breaths of dying Folds billowed around him despite the absence of wind!
He stood atop the emerging Primordial Stone Ape, whose undead form had grown even more terrifying since its transformation.
And leading them both, moving with the inexorable certainty of hunger given purpose...
Ozymandias!
The Purest Hunger had arrived, and reality itself held its breath!
Adui

chapters.title: Chapter 4176 Death! I
paragraphs: Above the skies of Concordia, where death and life were about to dance their eternal waltz, consciousness stirred within bones that had forgotten what flesh felt like.
"Ka Ka Ka!"
Arch Lich Ra'Zan's laughter erupted across dimensions like the sound of tombstones cracking under pressure!
Finally...finally!
He had been let loose on the battlefield with the Master once more! Freedom tasted like ash and possibility, like the moment between last breath and eternal silence.
The Master.

Ra'Zan's flaming eye sockets turned first to Ozymandias floating nearby...that manifestation of hunger so pure it made even death jealous...then to Noah in the distance, standing with arrogance among the panicking living!
How magnificent that the Master took on many forms! This time, he held the paradox of being both Living and Dead, walking in sunlight while casting shadows that belonged to tombs.
How glorious the Master was, to feel both life and death so freely, to taste existence from both sides of The Veil!

Ra'Zan himself much preferred death. Life was so... messy. All that breathing and hoping and feeling. Death, though...death was elegant in its finality. The essence of death felt comforting, like winter's embrace after a fever. Cold. Still. Home.

"Death," Ra'Zan mused to himself, his voice carrying the particular quality of someone having a delightful conversation at a party only they could attend, "is such a sweet release that many seek without knowing they seek it. Every risk taken, every war waged, every moment of despair...all roads leading to the same destination."
HUUM!
His skeletal jaw clicked in what might have been a grin.

"And I? I am merely a helpful guide, showing them the shortest path to where they were always going. Death isn't the enemy...it's the final punctuation mark on existence's rambling sentence. Without it, life would just go on and on, a run-on sentence that loses all meaning through sheer repetition!"
Of course, this entire tangent had occurred in less than a nanosecond of external time.
Ra'Zan could have lengthy debates with himself in the space between one moment and the next, exploring the nature of cessation while reality waited patiently for him to return.
But anyways- back to himself.

He was a record given identity by the gracious Master. One of many records that had been elevated from mere notation to genuine existence. He had even reached out to other Records under the Master...Hyperion that fat elephant, Commander Feng, Old Man Eudemus, OPPENHEIMER....

"Would you like to join me as The Dead?" he had asked them with genuine enthusiasm. "The benefits are eternal! No need for food, sleep, or those tedious biological functions. Plus, you get to experience existence from its most honest perspective- the end!"
WAA!
But those flimsy records were too prideful, too indecisive. They wanted to be called out on their own terms, to maintain their precious individuality.
Hmph. Let them rest in their delusions of independence. He would stand by his Master's side, delivering death with the dedication of an artist painting their masterpiece.
And his Master right now wanted more power.
Which meant, naturally, more death. Yes, his Master wanted endless death!
Not just any death...his Master wanted him to build a Legion.
Not a mere collection of undead puppets, but a true Legion of The Dead. A force that could withstand The Dead passing through The Veil, that could stand against the chaos about to unfold.
And that... Ra'Zan could give.
His gaze swept across the battlefield being born, taking in the Tears of Existence and The Dead emerging like poets from inspiration...sudden, dramatic, and likely to cause problems.
He also noted the astonishment of The Living, their faces painted with horror as they witnessed their worst nightmares taking physical form.
"Ah," he sighed wistfully, "if only the Master allowed me to taste these Living. How their life force would dance on my non-existent palate! But no, we're supposedly...allies."
For now.
He knew that at any moment, allies could become enemies...such was the nature of existence.

When that time came, he would love to sense death permeating across a Living Origin, watch it spread through a Living Elemental, taste the unique flavor each type of existence produced when it ceased.
Some deaths tasted sweet, like candy dissolving on a tongue he no longer possessed.
Some were bitter, like medicine that cured the disease of being. Others were simply euphoric, transcendent experiences that made even an undead consciousness dizzy with sensation.
But for now, he turned his flaming sockets away from the Living and toward The Dead emerging from tears that shouldn't exist.
His analysis was swift and methodical. The massive mummified existence above Concordia...five hundred trillion complexity, possibly more.
Noted for later consumption. The floating head of an Early Creature with its wings and tentacles...approaching quadrillion levels. Definitely a delicacy to be savored when the time was right.
He categorized each emergence with the efficiency of someone who had been organizing death for longer than most beings had been alive. High-priority targets, medium-priority targets, and then...
His skull snapped to the side, focusing on a particular tear that had just begun to widen. Through it emerged an obsidian Neanderthal, its form primitive yet terrifying in its simplicity.
Death swirled around it like a personal atmosphere, a storm of ending that made even other Dead Existences maintain respectful distance.
One hundred and sixty-six trillion complexity.
More powerful than a common Duke by sixteen times, yet this was the first Dead Existence that Ra'Zan set his sights on. Not the strongest, not the most impressive, but the most... suitable.

"Oh, little ape," he whispered through his link to the Primordial Stone Ape beneath him, his voice carrying the excitement of a child who had just spotted the perfect toy, "we have found the first minion for the Master's legion. Let us go!"
But as he prepared to launch himself toward glorious violence, something unprecedented occurred.
Through his bond with the Master, he sensed an exuberance of existence and power that made his flames burn brighter.
Prompts materialized before his vision...not the standard notifications but something grander, something that made even death pause to read.
|The Early Creature, Osmont's weavings of existence resonate due to confluence of factors|
|Unique authorities of all Living Existences contained within him paired with distinction as both Living and Dead|
|The Heart of an Early Creature is resonating with Seed of Principle of Perpetual Harvest|
|Unprecedented event manifesting: Birth of festival unseen even in the Earliest Folds|
|Through The Early Creature Osmont: HARVEST FESTIVAL OF DEATH shall bloom|
HUUM!
|Festival Parameters:|
|All Dead Existences under banner of The Early Creature: Power doubled|
|Mark of Perpetual Harvest of Death granted to allied Dead|
|Every creature (Living or Dead) turned to join ranks will have their Existence partially siphoned|
|Siphoned portions will be accumulated in Deathly Cache of Perpetual Harvest above Folds|
|At festival's end: Accumulated weavings amplified and distributed|
|Prize pools will result in a harvest of complexity and purity for The Early Creature, Osmont, and all participants|

chapters.title: Chapter 4177 Death! II
paragraphs: The euphoria that flooded through Ra'Zan's consciousness was beyond description!
Brilliant obsidian-green light erupted through his form, through the Ape beneath him, spreading across the entire Fold with subtlety that made it invisible to those not already marked.
His fifty trillion complexity instantly doubled!
One hundred trillion, just like that. The Primordial Stone Ape beneath him grew even more terrible, its capability to kill and permeate death elevated beyond previous limitations.
Ra'Zan's skull tilted back, and his voice rang out with titles that came from somewhere deeper than memory!

"O 9th Infernal Lord! O Tyrannical Lich Emperor! O Demon of the Seven Aeonic Havens! O Seeker of Apocalypse! O True Emperor of Necromancy!" His declaration made several nearby Living Existences stumble despite not being aimed at them.
"I...shall deliver to you a glorious Festival of Death!"
WU! WU! WU!
The promise carried weight that made reality document it, file it away as something that would definitely happen, no matter what forces might try to prevent it.
Below him, the Primordial Stone Ape beat its chest with arms that could shatter concepts, ready to charge toward their first target.
Above them, The Dead continued pouring through tears that multiplied with each passing moment.
And Ra'Zan? Ra'Zan was gloriously in his home element!
The Harvest Festival of Death had bloomed, and with it, Ra'Zan felt purpose crystallize into action.
His flaming gaze turned toward the obsidian Neanderthal, studying it with the particular attention of an artist selecting their canvas.
"I shall give us a nanosecond to handle that," he said to the Stone Ape beneath him, patting its massive shoulder with skeletal fingers that clicked against stone.
A nanosecond. For beings of their level, it might as well have been an eternity.
"Death is everywhere," Ra'Zan mused as he prepared to move. "In the space between heartbeats, in the pause between breaths, in the moment between thought and action. And where death exists, so do I."
The air was thick with Dead Existential Authority, making distance a mere suggestion.
Ra'Zan took a single step not through space but through death itself...and appeared behind the Neanderthal!
Simultaneously, the Primordial Stone Ape materialized in front, creating a perfect pincer.
Ra'Zan's enhanced perception, now doubled to one hundred trillion complexity, read the creature like an open book.
|Analyzing: Obsidian Neanderthal of Primordial Death|
|Classification: Dead Existence - Primitive Sovereign|
|Primary Authority: Dead Existential Authority|
|Special Trait: Devolution Field - Reduces complex structures to base components|
|Weakness: Still checking...|
|Threat Assessment: Manageable with current parameters|
The Primordial Stone Ape roared...a sound that made nearby tears in reality reconsider their stability.
Its newly elevated power of three hundred trillion complexity created shockwaves that served as perfect distraction!
The Neanderthal turned toward the obvious and most powerful threat, raising primitive fists that could unmake concepts through brute force alone.
Behind it, Ra'Zan moved with the silence of endings that hadn't been noticed yet.

His skull staff materialized in his grip...a weapon that was less object and more concentrated absence. He pushed it forward with gentle certainty, the staff bypassing layers of swirling Dead Existential Authority as if they were merely suggestions.
The moment it touched the Neanderthal's back, a branding erupted across its form...a flaming skull that bloomed like a flower of consumption.
The mark didn't burn; it devoured, feeding on the Dead Existential Authority with hunger that transcended physical appetite!
The Neanderthal tried to turn, to fight, but the Stone Ape's massive arms clamped down in a bear hug that redefined the concept of restraint!
The Ape's body erupted with its own devouring light...hunger meeting death in an embrace that neither could escape.

"While you are The Dead," Ra'Zan said conversationally, as if discussing weather while reality writhed, "we are Dead Existential Inevitabilities. We have death... and Hunger as well. And that, my dear Neanderthal, you cannot match against."
WAA!
The devouring continued with mechanical precision. Authority flowed from the Neanderthal into its attackers like water finding its level!
The creature's form began to dim, its primitive features becoming translucent as existence itself was being negotiated away.
"Stop."
Ra'Zan's command halted everything.
The Stone Ape released its grip, stepping back as the nearly collapsed Neanderthal swayed but remained standing...barely.
Prompts cascaded before Ra'Zan's vision:
|Successfully hungered and devoured: 40 Trillion Transferable Complexity|
|Distribution: 15 Trillion to Arch Lich Ra'Zan|
|15 Trillion to Primordial Stone Ape|
|10 Trillion to The Early Creature, Osmont|
|Current Complexity: Ra'Zan - 130 Trillion(Amplified)|
The numbers were glorious, but Ra'Zan wasn't finished. The Neanderthal stood there, unable to move, one push away from perishing...which meant returning in a day, starting the cycle anew.

"No," Ra'Zan said, his voice carrying the weight of revelation. "I will not let you or any of the others die. After all, it is not really death since you will come back. That's not death...that's just... inconvenience."
He raised his staff, its tip glowing with purpose that transcended destruction.

"I will use you. I will transform you. You see, I have an ability which allows me to summon Dead Existences. But they would be weak echoes, or I would have to give them portions of my power." His skull tilted with what might have been disgust. "And I... do not want to give. In this grand symphony of death, I take!"
HUUM!
The staff plunged into the Neanderthal's chest with the certainty of fate acknowledging itself.
"So I shall take your existence and transform it as the base. Come! Arise! Summon... The Dead!"
Obsidian smoke erupted, not from the wound but from existence itself acknowledging fundamental change.
The Neanderthal's massive body trembled, then began breaking down into possibility!
The transformation was neither gentle nor violent; it simply was, with the inevitability of death itself.
From the swirling storm of Dead Existential Authority...
"KAAA!"
A new aura blazed to life, different yet familiar, changed yet recognizable.
|Rare Dead Existence Successfully Summoned from Compatible Material|
|Entity: Neanderthal Jiangshi - Hopping Corpse of Primitive Force|
|Complexity: 75,000,000,000,000(75 Trillion)|
|Special Traits: Retains 45% original power, Gains "Hopping Thunder" mobility|
|Loyalty: Absolute to Summoner|
|Classification: First Minion of the Legion. Low Ranking The Dead|

He raised his staff, its tip glowing with purpose that transcended destruction.
"I will use you.
I will transform you.
You see, I have an ability which allows me to summon Dead Existences.
But they would be weak echoes, or I would have to give them portions of my power." His skull tilted with what might have been disgust.
"And I... do not want to give.
In this grand symphony of death, I take!"
HUUM!
The staff plunged into the Neanderthal's chest with the certainty of fate acknowledging itself.
"So I shall take your existence and transform it as the base.
Come!
Arise!
Summon...
The Dead!"
Obsidian smoke erupted, not from the wound but from existence itself acknowledging fundamental change.
The Neanderthal's massive body trembled, then began breaking down into possibility!
The transformation was neither gentle nor violent; it simply was, with the inevitability of death itself.
From the swirling storm of Dead Existential Authority...
"KAAA!"
A new aura blazed to life, different yet familiar, changed yet recognizable.
|Rare Dead Existence Successfully Summoned from Compatible Material|
|Entity: Neanderthal Jiangshi - Hopping Corpse of Primitive Force|
|Complexity: 75,000,000,000,000(75 Trillion)|
|Special Traits: Retains 45% original power, Gains "Hopping Thunder" mobility|
|Loyalty: Absolute to Summoner|
|Classification: First Minion of the Legion.
Low Ranking The Dead|

chapters.title: Chapter 4178 Death! III
paragraphs: The newly transformed creature knelt...an awkward motion for something designed for primitive violence, yet it managed with newfound grace!
The Legion of The Dead had truly begun!
"Ka Ka Ka!" Ra'Zan's laughter rang out across the battlefield with the joy of someone who had just discovered their favorite hobby could also be their profession.
Below in Concordia, Living Existences watched in mounting horror.

From their perspective, tears had opened, Dead Existences had emerged...terrifying but expected. But now? Now one Dead Existence had attacked another, devoured its power, then transformed it into something else entirely!
Something loyal to purposes they couldn't fathom.
Duke Visana of the Living Elementals actually took a step back. "What in the collapsed Folds is that thing doing?! Are they all mindless?!"
Were they mindless?
Haha...KaKa!
What did these dumb fuckers know?!
Their worries were distant music to Ra'Zan's consciousness. He turned his burning gaze toward the battles beginning across the Folds, seeing opportunity where others saw catastrophe.
"Master," he bellowed with joy that made death itself uncomfortable, "that was only the first! Many more will come!"

Without pause, Ra'Zan moved...he, the Stone Ape, and the Neanderthal Jiangshi taking a single synchronized step through death to appear around another Dead Existence near a different tear. This one radiated two hundred and fifty trillion complexity, its form a writhing mass of tentacles and regret.
The second target writhed with tentacles that redefined geometry, its squid-like body pulsing with colors that shouldn't exist.
Ra'Zan studied it with the appreciation of someone examining a particularly interesting corpse...before making it one.
|Analyzing: Chthonian Horror of the Sunken Depths|
|Classification: Dead Existence - Abyssal Sovereign|
|Primary Authority: Dead Existential Autjority, Curse-Woven Death, Miasmic Corruption|
|Special Traits: Reality Decay Field, Corpse Manipulation|
|Warning: Some intelligence detected|
This one had noticed them. More concerning, other Dead Existences throughout the Folds had begun to take notice of them.
The element of surprise...such a living concept anyway, was gone!
The Chthonian Horror moved first.

Its tentacles whipped through space, but not to strike...to write. Each movement inscribed curses into reality itself, making the air become poison, making space become trap, making time become molasses.
The miasma that erupted from its form wasn't merely toxic; it was the concept of corruption given gaseous form.
"Oh, how delightful!" Ra'Zan exclaimed as his bones began to dissolve at the edges!
The Primordial Stone Ape roared and charged, but walls erupted to block its path...not stone or metal, but flesh.
Carcass Inducement manifested as waves of corpses that had never lived, bodies that existed only to have died, surging forward in putrid tsunamis!
The Ape's fists connected with wet impacts that made reality gag.
"Master always said," Ra'Zan mused while dodging a tentacle that rewrote the definition of his location, "that death should be artistic. But this? This is just showing off."
The Neanderthal Jiangshi attempted to hop through...its primitive form enhanced with thunderous impacts, but each landing spawned more corpse-waves!
The nearby battlefield had become an ocean of endings that hadn't happened to anyone specific, death without the courtesy of prior life.

Ra'Zan's skull tilted as he analyzed the situation. Raw power wouldn't work here...the creature had turned the entire area into its domain. But domains were just another form of structure, and structure could be understood, exploited, devoured.
"You know what your problem is?" Ra'Zan called out conversationally while his staff manifested. "You're trying to use death as a wall. Death isn't a wall...it's a door. And doors..."
He tapped his staff against the miasma itself. Where it touched, the corruption didn't disappear...it inverted, becoming a pathway.
"Doors open both ways."
HUUM!
The Primordial Stone Ape understood immediately. Instead of fighting through the corpse-waves, it began devouring them.

Each body consumed added fractional power, but more importantly, created gaps in the creature's defense. The Neanderthal Jiangshi hopped through these gaps with thunderous impacts that scattered the reformed flesh.
BOOM! BOOM!
The Chthonian Horror writhed, its tentacles accelerating their curse-writing.

New abilities manifested...Entropy Cascade that aged everything in proximity, Soul Reef that created barriers from spirits that had never existed, Null Depth that tried to drag everything into an abyss that was also somehow here!

"Your understanding of death is comprehensive," Ra'Zan admitted while using his complexity to simply tank through an Entropy Cascade that would have aged wheels to dust. "But it's also limited. You see death as ending, as cessation, as wall between is and isn't."
He appeared beside the creature through a doorway made from its own miasma.
"I see death as transformation. As possibility. As the moment where everything becomes everything else."

His staff touched the creature's main body. The branding that erupted wasn't a single skull but a constellation of them, each one keyed to a different aspect of death the creature wielded. The Horror's own mastery became the keys to its locks.
The Primordial Stone Ape, now close enough, wrapped its arms around the mass of tentacles in a grip that redefined restraint. Three hundred trillion complexity focused into pure hungering strength!
The Neanderthal Jiangshi hopped onto the creature's top, its primitive fury adding weight that transcended physical mass.
"Death is my domain," Ra'Zan said as the devouring reached its crescendo. "You're just visiting."
BOOM!
|Successfully hungered and devoured: 100 Trillion Transferable Complexity|
|Distribution: 35 Trillion to Arch Lich Ra'Zan|
|35 Trillion to Primordial Stone Ape|
|20 Trillion to The Early Creature, Osmont|
|10 Trillion to Neanderthal Jiangshi|
|Current Complexity: Ra'Zan - 200 Trillion|

The Chthonian Horror's form had dimmed to near-transparency, its tentacles barely maintaining cohesion. Ra'Zan studied it with the particular attention of someone about to perform delicate surgery with a sledgehammer.
"Your curse-weaving capabilities are exquisite," he said, raising his staff. "It would be a shame to lose them. So let's not. Summon... The Dead!"
HUUM!
The transformation was more violent this time...the creature had more complexity to restructure, more abilities to preserve.
Tentacles writhed and reformed, the squid body compressing and expanding simultaneously!
When the smoke cleared...
|A glorious Dead Existence has been Summoned|
|Entity: Abyssal Lich-Kraken of Cursed Depths|
|Special Traits: Retains Curse-Weaving, Gains Lich's Magical Arsenal|
|Unique Ability: Can transform between squid and humanoid lich forms|
|Loyalty: Absolute to Summoner|
The new creature that emerged was magnificent in its impossibility!
In one moment it was a kraken of shadows and curses, in the next a robed lich with tentacles for fingers. It knelt, somehow, despite its ever-shifting form.
"Welcome to the Legion," Ra'Zan said cheerfully.
Below, the weak Living Existences and Fold Dwellers had gone from horror to something beyond...a kind of numb acceptance that reality had decided to stop making sense.

Dukes...had somber expressions as they were already forced to move, with the more powerful Dead Existences- the mummufied creature and the head of An Early Creature, had begun devouring everything around them!
Ra'Zan surveyed his growing Legion...two members, the fat Ape, and counting. His gaze swept across the battlefield where hundreds more Dead Existences emerged from tears that kept multiplying!
So many candidates. So many possibilities for transformation!

chapters.title: Chapter 4179 Do Not Fear, Young One I
paragraphs: Noah gazed at the darkening space above Concordia, his eyes pulsing with delight at the systematic harvest Ra'Zan was conducting.
Each transformation, each addition to the Legion, represented exponential growth in a game where exponential was the minimum acceptable rate of advancement.
This place, this moment of chaos and emergence, was a grand weaving of possibility!
Where others saw catastrophe, he saw opportunity wrapped in violence.
Prompts materialized before his vision, documenting the accumulating benefits:
|Harvest Festival of Death Progress:|
|Dead Existences joined ranks: 2|
|Existential weavings siphoned to Deathly Cache: 28% of original essences|
|Cache accumulation rate: Increasing|
|Current participants: (You, Ra'Zan, Primordial Stone Ape, Ozymandias...)|
His gaze rose to track what the prompts described.
Far above, barely visible through the tears and chaos, an illusory chest floated...the Deathly Cache of Perpetual Harvest.
It pulsed with obsidian-gold light, each pulse seeming to whisper that he simply needed to outperform, to harvest more, and the rewards would scale beyond current imagination.

Power coursed through his body with each successful hunt Ra'Zan completed. Every decimated Dead Existence sent trillions of complexity flowing...half to him, half to Ozymandias, though it was all designated under The Early Creature, Osmont.
The distribution was automatic, efficient, perfect.
His complexity had already grown by factors that would have taken others eons to achieve!
Things were proceeding smoothly, perhaps too smoothly, which should have been his first warning.
But as someone had said recently, someone whose name carried weight...
"Existence is unfair..."
Existence was unfair. Always!
The words had barely formed in his thoughts when...
BOOM!
Space fractured.
No.

Space surrendered! The sound was wrong, carrying frequencies that predated the invention of sound, that made reality question whether it wanted to continue existing in proximity to whatever had just arrived!
Noah's heart hammered once...a single beat that his enhanced perception stretched into eternity.

His eyes flashed with solemnity as understanding crystallized: something beyond current parameters had arrived! His hands moved with speed that transcended thought, wrapping around Sigrid with protective certainty.
Ozymandias appeared behind him instantaneously, not traveling through space but simply editing his location!
Ra'Zan and his Legion stepped through death itself, ignoring concepts like distance or obstacles to materialize in defensive positions around their Master.
Then impact came!
BOOM!
They didn't see what caused it...that was perhaps the most terrifying part.
It ignored speed because it had already arrived before departing. It ignored distance because it existed in many places simultaneously!
All Noah perceived was a column of obsidian light shooting down from a crack that shouldn't have existed, carrying within it the weight of endings that had been waiting too long to be gentle.
Then came decimation.
The word was insufficient.
Languages hadn't evolved terms for what happened when existence itself was used as a weapon against those existing within it!
Noah felt his body subjected to battering that came from all directions and none, impacts that existed in past, present, and future simultaneously.
|WARNING: Affected by Overpowering Haki|
|Source complexity of Haki: >10 Quadrillion|
|All abilities and power reduced by 50%|
|Decimation attempt on surrounding environment detected: 1 Quadrillion complexity deployed against your existence|
|Mitigation occurring:|
|- 40% absorbed by Dead Existential Inevitabilities' hunger|
|- 15% dispersed by Order's eruption|
|- 20% negated by your own Complexity/Purity|
|- 25% unmitigated - BRACE FOR IMPACT|
BOOM!
BOOM!
The battering continued, each wave trying to convince his atoms they had never been properly assembled.
His bones creaked with pressure that could compress Wheels into singularities! Beside him, Sigrid's Order authority blazed in desperate defense, trying to maintain structure against pure decimation!
More prompts, each one worse than the last.
|Damage Assessment: Critical but Survivable|
|Neanderthal Jiangshi has collapsed existence to preserve Master|
|Return time: 12 hours|
|Abyssal Lich-Kraken has sacrificed totality under Ra'Zan's command|
|Return time: 10 hours|
Two members of his newly raised Legion- gone. Not destroyed, but forced to cease existing temporarily just to ensure his survival!
Finally, after what felt like epochs but had been mere seconds, the assault ended.
The thick obsidian dust that had replaced air began to clear, revealing devastation that redefined the term.
Half of Ra'Zan's body simply wasn't there anymore...not destroyed but negated, his bones ending in smooth surfaces as if reality had been edited.
The Primordial Stone Ape's entire left shoulder had been decimated, the missing mass creating an asymmetry that shouldn't have allowed it to remain standing.

Ozymandias had transformed into something that barely maintained coherent form...a pulsing mass of tentacles that writhed with desperate hunger, trying to devour enough ambient energy to maintain existence.
|Survival of Unsurvivable Impact Confirmed|
|Tremendous effort recognized by Principle of Perpetual Harvest|
|Complexity gained: +1 Trillion|
|Purity gained: +1 Trillion|
The prompt was a boon, but it felt like being handed a bandage after being shot with a cannon. Because as the dust settled further, the true scope of devastation became clear!
Aeternitas Concordia...that golden jewel of commerce and cooperation, was rubble.
The elaborate towers that had stood for eons had been reduced to scattered blocks, their golden surfaces tarnished with shadows of death that moved independently of light.

Bridges that had connected impossible architectures now dangled like broken fingers. The grand marketplace where he had been trading mere minutes ago was a crater that went deeper than geography should allow.
But worse than the structural damage were the casualties.
Every Fold Dweller and Living Existence that had been near Noah was now a twitching skeleton wrapped in flesh that hadn't gotten the message it was supposed to be dead.
Every single one.
Their bodies radiated malformed auras of death, caught between states in ways that made The Dead look healthy by comparison!
They weren't alive, but they weren't properly dead either...trapped in a liminal space that existence hadn't created categories for.
Following the weavings of decimation like a trail of breadcrumbs made from catastrophe, Noah and Sigrid's gazes found the epicenter.
An Early Creature stood there.
Oh!
An Early Creature radiating Trillion of Complexity stood in the midst of utter devastation as her arrival alone killed everything!
